@@@=== FILE START: README.md ===
# xml-toolkit

A Java toolkit with two core commands, wrapped in a REST API and a web UI:

- **generate**: reads an XSD and writes realistic, XSD-valid sample XMLs -- content levels,
  size tiers, deliberate error injection, DTCC supplement embedding, parallel generation, and a
  full JSON/CSV report.
- **infer**: reads a folder of sample XMLs and writes a best-guess XSD plus a plain-language,
  confidence-ranked review report.

Three Maven modules under the `message-platform` parent, plus a frontend:

```
message-platform/
  pom.xml                   parent (packaging=pom)
  xsd/                      4 real ISO 20022 sample XSDs
  xml-toolkit/              the engine (CLI) -- generate / infer / scan
  xml-toolkit-api/          Spring Boot 3 REST API wrapping the engine
  xml-toolkit-ui/           React + TypeScript + Vite frontend for the API
```

---

## Setting up on a new machine (first time only)

Follow these steps in order. Each one assumes the previous one finished successfully.

### 1. Install prerequisites

| Tool | Minimum version | Check it's installed and on PATH |
|---|---|---|
| Java (a JDK, not just a JRE) | 17 or newer | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.6 or newer | `mvn -version` |
| Node.js | 18 or newer | `node -v` |
| npm | comes bundled with Node | `npm -v` |

Run each check command in a terminal. If any of them says "command not found" (or similar),
install that tool before continuing -- everything below depends on all four being available.

### 2. Get the project onto the machine

Copy the whole project folder over -- the one containing this `README.md`, `pom.xml`, `xsd/`,
`xml-toolkit/`, `xml-toolkit-api/`, `xml-toolkit-ui/`. You do **not** need to bring:

- `target/` folders inside `xml-toolkit/` or `xml-toolkit-api/` -- rebuilt by step 3
- `node_modules/` or `dist/` inside `xml-toolkit-ui/` -- rebuilt by step 5
- `xml-toolkit-api-data/` -- the backend recreates this itself the first time it runs (see
  [Where everything gets stored](#where-everything-gets-stored) below)
- `generated/` or `inferred/` if present -- these are just leftover output from manually running
  the CLI, not part of the project itself

Leaving those out just means a smaller copy; bringing them along by accident won't break
anything either.

### 3. Build the Java side (engine + API)

Open a terminal **at the project root** (the folder with `pom.xml` in it) and run:

```bash
mvn clean package
```

This compiles both `xml-toolkit` (the engine) and `xml-toolkit-api` (the REST API) and runs
their test suites. It should end with `BUILD SUCCESS`. Afterward you'll have:

- `xml-toolkit/target/xml-toolkit.jar`
- `xml-toolkit-api/target/xml-toolkit-api.jar`

You only need to repeat this step after changing Java code (see
[Rebuilding](#rebuilding-after-changing-java-code) below for the one thing to watch out for).

### 4. Start the backend

Still from the **project root** (this matters -- see the note below):

```bash
java -jar xml-toolkit-api/target/xml-toolkit-api.jar
```

Leave this terminal open; it's your running server. It listens on `http://localhost:8080`.

> **Always start it from the project root.** The backend stores its data in a folder named
> `xml-toolkit-api-data`, created automatically relative to wherever you launch the `java -jar`
> command from. Launch it from a different folder and it'll create a second, separate (empty)
> data folder there instead -- confusingly, with your schemas/history missing. One terminal
> starting point, every time, avoids that.

### 5. Build and start the frontend

Open a **second terminal** (leave the backend's terminal running):

```bash
cd xml-toolkit-ui
npm install
npm run dev
```

`npm install` downloads the frontend's dependencies and only needs to run once (or again after
`package.json` changes). `npm run dev` starts the UI on `http://localhost:5173` and
automatically forwards its `/api/*` calls to the backend on port 8080 -- no extra configuration
needed, as long as the backend from step 4 is already running.

### 6. Open the app

**http://localhost:5173/**

You'll start with an empty Registry and History (this is a fresh install) -- use the **Generate
XMLs** or **Create XSD** page to upload/register an XSD and get going. Four sample ISO 20022
XSDs are already in the `xsd/` folder if you want something to try immediately.

---

## Everyday use (after the first setup)

Every time you come back to work on this:

```bash
# Terminal 1 -- from the project root
java -jar xml-toolkit-api/target/xml-toolkit-api.jar

# Terminal 2
cd xml-toolkit-ui
npm run dev
```

(No `npm install` needed again unless `package.json` changed, and no `mvn package` needed again
unless the Java code changed.) Open `http://localhost:5173/`. Stop either one with `Ctrl+C` in
its own terminal when you're done.

### Rebuilding after changing Java code

**Stop the backend first** (`Ctrl+C` in its terminal), *then* run `mvn clean package`. Maven's
`clean` step deletes the old `xml-toolkit-api.jar` before rebuilding it, and Windows (and most
OSes) won't let it delete a file that a running `java` process still has open. If you forget and
see an error like:

```
Failed to execute goal ... clean ... Failed to delete ...xml-toolkit-api.jar
```

it means the backend from a previous session is still running somewhere. Stop it, then re-run
`mvn clean package`.

### "Web server failed to start. Port 8080 was already in use."

This means a backend is already running (maybe you forgot to stop a previous one, or started it
twice). Find and stop it:

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='java.exe'" | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*xml-toolkit-api*' } | Select-Object ProcessId
Stop-Process -Id <id> -Force
```

**macOS / Linux:**
```bash
lsof -i :8080
kill <pid>
```

Then start the backend again.

### "500 Internal Server Error" on the Registry or History page

This almost always means the frontend (port 5173) is running but the backend (port 8080) isn't
-- the dev server's proxy can't reach it and reports it as a 500 instead of a clearer "can't
connect" message. Make sure the backend from step 4 above is actually running and listening on
port 8080, then refresh the page.

---

## Where everything gets stored

| Folder | What's in it | Safe to delete? |
|---|---|---|
| `xml-toolkit-api-data/` | The running app's real data: `registry.json` (registered schemas), `schemas/` (their uploaded `.xsd` bytes), `history.json` (past runs), `jobs/<job-id>/` (each run's generated zip / inferred XSD / reports) -- everything you see in the Registry and History pages lives here | Yes, but you lose all registered schemas and history. The backend recreates an empty one automatically next time it starts -- there's no way to run it without this folder reappearing, it just starts empty. |
| `xml-toolkit/target/`, `xml-toolkit-api/target/` | Maven build output (compiled classes, the runnable jars) | Yes -- `mvn clean package` regenerates it |
| `xml-toolkit-ui/node_modules/`, `xml-toolkit-ui/dist/` | npm dependencies / production build output | Yes -- `npm install` / `npm run build` regenerate them |
| `generated/`, `inferred/` (if present) | Output from manually running the CLI (`java -jar xml-toolkit.jar generate/infer ...`) directly, outside the app | Yes -- not referenced by any code; purely wherever you pointed `--out` |

Normal use through the UI never touches `generated/` or `inferred/` at all -- everything goes
through `xml-toolkit-api-data/jobs/` and comes back to you via the Download buttons in the
browser.

---

## Build everything (reference)

```bash
mvn clean package
```

Builds all three Maven modules and runs the Java test suite (engine + API). Run just the tests
with `mvn clean test`.

To build only one module (plus whatever it depends on), use `-pl <module> -am`, e.g.
`mvn -pl xml-toolkit-api -am package`.

## The engine: `xml-toolkit/target/xml-toolkit.jar`

### generate (XSD -> XMLs)

```bash
java -jar xml-toolkit/target/xml-toolkit.jar generate \
  --xsd xsd/SomeMessage.xsd --out generated/SomeMessage \
  --count 1000 --size mixed --seed 42
```

| Flag | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `--xsd` | input XSD | required |
| `--out` | output folder, or the zip file path when `--output zip` | required unless `--output stream` |
| `--count` | how many XML files | `1000` |
| `--size` | `small`\|`medium`\|`large`\|`mixed` -- only matters at `--level 3` | `mixed` |
| `--seed` | same seed -> byte-identical output | random |
| `--level` | `1` required-only, `2` required+optional, `3` +repetitions | `3` |
| `--profile` | YAML file overriding name-based value rules (e.g. `PlcAndNm` -> an element path, not a person name) | `xml-toolkit/profiles/default.yaml` behavior built in |
| `--threads` | generation thread pool size | all CPU cores |
| `--output` | `folder`\|`zip`\|`stream` (stream writes a zip byte stream to stdout) | `folder` |
| `--error-percent` / `--error-types` | inject exactly one deliberate, validation-failing error into that percent of files, from the given types (comma list; default: every type the schema supports) | `0` (off) |
| `--supplement` | another XSD to generate a valid document for and embed inside every `xs:any` slot (e.g. seev.035 -> supl.009), independently validated against its own schema first | none |

Every run writes `report.json`/`report.csv` (settings, seed, counts, size stats, time,
files/sec) and `manifest.json`/`manifest.csv` (one row per file: valid, or which error was
injected and where) alongside the output.

Use `java -jar xml-toolkit.jar scan --xsd <file>` to see what a schema actually contains
(required/optional/choice/enum/pattern counts, which error types it supports) before generating.

### infer (XMLs -> XSD)

```bash
java -jar xml-toolkit/target/xml-toolkit.jar infer \
  --xml generated/SomeMessage --out inferred/SomeMessage.xsd [--baseline previous.xsd]
```

Writes the inferred XSD plus `<name>_review.md` and `<name>_review.json` next to it -- only the
genuinely doubtful calls (low sample count, a near-unanimous one-occurrence split, a real
enumeration/choice candidate), each tagged with a confidence level; everything high-confidence is
auto-accepted and just counted, not listed. `--baseline` switches the report to only the
differences from a previously-written XSD.

---

## The API: `xml-toolkit-api`

```bash
java -jar xml-toolkit-api/target/xml-toolkit-api.jar
```

Starts on `http://localhost:8080` with sensible defaults (data stored in `./xml-toolkit-api-data`
relative to wherever you launch it from). To override them:

```bash
java -jar xml-toolkit-api/target/xml-toolkit-api.jar \
  --app.allowed-base-folders=/path/to/a/safe/folder \
  --app.data-dir=./xml-toolkit-api-data
```

`app.allowed-base-folders` is the whitelist a server-side path (schema upload target, infer
`serverPath` input) must resolve inside -- only needed if you use the "server path" input mode.
`app.data-dir` is where the registry, job output, decisions, and history are persisted (created
automatically if missing).

Endpoints: `/api/schemas` (list/register/scan/download), `/api/generate` + `/api/jobs/{id}`
(status, SSE events, cancel, download, report), `/api/infer` (zip/files/serverPath upload) +
`/api/infer/{id}/{groups,review,decisions,register,xsd}`, `/api/history` (+ rerun). See the
controller classes under `xml-toolkit-api/src/main/java/.../api/controller` for exact request/
response shapes.

Known limitation: `POST /api/infer/{jobId}/decisions` records a human's decision and won't
re-ask about it on a later run, but doesn't yet rewrite the XSD from most decision kinds (the
engine doesn't support that yet) -- the response says so explicitly.

## The UI: `xml-toolkit-ui`

```bash
cd xml-toolkit-ui
npm install
npm run dev        # http://localhost:5173, proxies /api to http://localhost:8080
```

Needs the API running (above) at `localhost:8080` -- the dev server proxies `/api/*` to it (see
`vite.config.ts`). `npm run build` produces a static `dist/` you can serve from anything; `npm
test` runs the Vitest unit/component suite.

Four pages (top nav): **Generate XMLs** (pick/upload a schema, settings, live sample preview,
SSE progress, result card with download/report/save-as-profile), **Create XSD** (folder picker
with in-browser grouping+sampling, ZIP upload, or server path; group-by-group review with
accept/reject decisions and rebuild; download/register), **Registry** (every registered schema,
its scan summary, download), **History** (past runs, re-run).

---

## A note on the real XSDs used here

The 4 XSDs checked into `xsd/` are real ISO 20022 "corporate action" message schemas (SWIFT/DTCC
2025 standard release): `seev.035` / `seev.036` (preliminary advice / confirmation) and their
`supl.009` / `supl.011` DTCC supplementary extensions. They're large (71-227 declared elements
each), self-contained (no `xs:import`/`xs:include` between them), and use `Document` as the single
root element in each case.

See `xml-toolkit/REVIEW_FACTS.md` for the original factual engine review, including the before/
after numbers for the infer-mode fixes (round-trip validation on 50 real seev.035 samples went
from 1/50 to 50/50, and inferred complexType count from 183 down to 89, against the original
schema's own 95).

#   xpath  -- a path to another element of the same message (e.g. /Document/CorpActnGnlInf),

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/REVIEW_FACTS.md ===
# xml-toolkit — Factual Review

Prepared by reading the source in `xml-toolkit/src/` and running the built jar. No code was changed.
All file/line references are in `xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/`.

**Deviation from the original request:** section 3 was specified as `--count 1000` per XSD. On this
machine that measured ~0.4–0.5 files/sec for the two largest schemas (seev.035/seev.036), i.e. a
projected ~35–40 min for those two alone. The user explicitly chose to reduce this to `--count 200`
per XSD (same `--size mixed --seed 42`) to keep the review timely. This is noted wherever it matters.

---

## 1. Build and libraries

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Maven | Apache Maven 3.9.9, running on JDK 24.0.2 (Oracle) |
| `java` on PATH (runs the built jar) | 19.0.1 (2022-10-18), HotSpot 64-Bit |
| `maven.compiler.release` (parent `pom.xml`) | 17 |

**Parent `pom.xml`** (`com.project:message-platform:1.0.0`, `packaging=pom`): declares no
`<dependencies>` — it only lists `<module>xml-toolkit</module>` and the compiler-release property.

**`xml-toolkit/pom.xml`** full `<dependencies>`:

| groupId | artifactId | version | scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| org.apache.ws.xmlschema | xmlschema-core | 2.3.1 | compile |
| org.junit.jupiter | junit-jupiter | 5.10.2 | test |

`mvn dependency:tree` shows `xmlschema-core:2.3.1` has **zero transitive dependencies** — no
Woodstox, no Aalto, no stax2-api. The junit-jupiter test dependency pulls in the usual
junit-jupiter-api/params/engine, opentest4j, junit-platform-commons/engine, apiguardian-api (all
test scope only).

**StAX implementation actually used at runtime.** Confirmed by loading the built fat jar
(`xml-toolkit/target/xml-toolkit.jar`, produced by `maven-shade-plugin`) on the classpath and
calling the factory methods directly:

```
XMLInputFactory.newFactory()   = com.sun.xml.internal.stream.XMLInputFactoryImpl
XMLInputFactory.newInstance()  = com.sun.xml.internal.stream.XMLInputFactoryImpl
XMLOutputFactory.newFactory()  = com.sun.xml.internal.stream.XMLOutputFactoryImpl
XMLOutputFactory.newInstance() = com.sun.xml.internal.stream.XMLOutputFactoryImpl
```

This is the **JDK's built-in StAX implementation** (`com.sun.xml.internal.stream`), not Woodstox or
Aalto — consistent with the dependency tree having no StAX implementation jar on the classpath.
Both `GenerateCommand` and `XmlStructureScanner` call `XMLOutputFactory.newInstance()` /
`XMLInputFactory.newInstance()` with no vendor-specific property set (`XmlStructureScanner.java:30`
sets only `IS_COALESCING`), so there is no code path that could pick a different implementation
even if one were on the classpath.

---

## 2. Generate mode: how it works

| Responsibility | Class (file) |
|---|---|
| Parse XSD, find root `Document` element | `SchemaIndex` (`generate/SchemaIndex.java`) |
| Resolve a simple type's restriction chain to its built-in base + merged facets | `SimpleTypeResolver` (`generate/SimpleTypeResolver.java`) → `ResolvedSimpleType` |
| Walk the type tree and stream XML via StAX | `XmlInstanceGenerator` (`generate/XmlInstanceGenerator.java`) |
| Produce leaf text values | `ValueGenerator` (`generate/ValueGenerator.java`) |
| Sample strings matching an `xs:pattern` | `XsdPatternSampler` (`generate/XsdPatternSampler.java`) |
| Orchestrate per-tier calibration, per-file retry loop, CLI options/results | `GenerateCommand` / `GenerateOptions` / `GenerateResult` (`generate/`) |
| Validate a written file against the XSD | `XsdValidatorCache` (`validate/XsdValidatorCache.java`), shared with infer mode |

**Reuse of expensive objects** — created once per run, not per file:
- `XMLOutputFactory outputFactory = XMLOutputFactory.newInstance();` — `GenerateCommand.java:40`, created once before the per-tier calibration loop and passed into every `writeOne`/`trialSize` call for the whole run.
- The compiled `javax.xml.validation.Schema` is cached in a `ConcurrentHashMap<Path, Schema>` keyed by XSD path (`XsdValidatorCache.java:21,27`) — compiled once the first time a given XSD path is validated against, reused for every subsequent file (and reused again by infer mode's post-validation step).
- The repeat factor needed to hit a size tier's byte target is calibrated once per `(XSD, tier)` pair per run (`GenerateCommand.java:45-48`), not recalculated per file.
- `SchemaIndex` (the parsed `XmlSchemaCollection`) is built once per run and shared by every file write (`GenerateCommand.java:33`, passed into `XmlInstanceGenerator`).
- Not reused across files: a fresh `SimpleTypeResolver` and `ValueGenerator` are constructed per `XmlInstanceGenerator` instance, i.e. per file write and per calibration trial (`XmlInstanceGenerator.java:38-39`). `SimpleTypeResolver` has its own internal cache, but that cache does not survive past one file/trial.

**Threading.** Single-threaded. `GenerateCommand.run` is one sequential `for` loop over the file
plan (`GenerateCommand.java:54`); no `ExecutorService`, `Thread`, or parallel stream appears
anywhere in `generate/` or `validate/`.

**Pattern (`xs:pattern`) sampling.** Custom hand-rolled sampler, not a regex library
(`XsdPatternSampler.java`). It parses the pattern into a small AST (alternation → concat →
quantified → atom) and samples from that tree.

| Supported | Not supported |
|---|---|
| Literals | Anchors `^` `$` (parsed as plain literal characters, not treated specially) |
| Grouping `( ... )` | Backreferences |
| Alternation `\|` | Lookahead / lookbehind |
| Quantifiers `?` `*` `+` `{n}` `{n,m}` `{n,}` | Non-greedy quantifiers (`*?`, `+?`, `??`) |
| Character classes `[...]`, ranges `a-z`, negation `[^...]` | Unicode property escapes (`\p{L}` etc.) |
| Shorthands `\d` `\w` (and `\s` mapped to a literal space) | `\D`, `\W`, `\S` (negated shorthands fall through to `shorthand()`'s default branch, which treats the escaped letter as a literal character, e.g. `\S` samples as the literal character `S`) |
| `.` (mapped to `[A-Za-z0-9]`, not "any character") | — |

For unquantified `*`/`+`, the sampler picks a bounded random repeat count (`*` → 0–5, `+` → 1–5,
`{n,}` → `n`–`n+5`) rather than an unbounded one (`Quantified` record, lines 59-85). Negated
character classes `[^...]` sample from a fixed alphanumeric fallback set and reject matches found
in the excluded ranges, retrying up to 20 times (lines 216-233). For non-negated classes that mix
letters/digits with other characters (e.g. typical SWIFT "x"-charset patterns), it biases 85% of
samples toward the alphanumeric-only subset of the ranges (`alnumRanges()`, line 209) so output
reads as words rather than punctuation noise — but the other ~15% of the time it samples the full
declared class including punctuation. This is visible in the generated output (section 3) as
occasional values like `pp00tQDw7/L` or `61S'Z7uUf3yd2't1o`.

**`xs:any` handling.** `writeAnyFiller()` (`XmlInstanceGenerator.java:189-193`) always writes the
exact same fixed stub, regardless of the `xs:any`'s `namespace`/`processContents` attributes:
```xml
<ExtensionData>supplementary-data</ExtensionData>
```
In `seev.035` and `seev.036`, the only `xs:any` in each schema (`namespace="##any"
processContents="lax"`) sits inside `complexType SupplementaryDataEnvelope1`, which is the type of
element `Envlp`, which is itself the sole child of the repeatable `SplmtryData` element
(`SplmtryData` → `Envlp` → `xs:any`). So generated output always contains:
```xml
<ns:SplmtryData><ns:Envlp><ExtensionData>supplementary-data</ExtensionData></ns:Envlp></ns:SplmtryData>
```
(confirmed in the sample shown in section 3). `ExtensionData` is written with no namespace prefix
(the ambient default/no namespace), which the schema's `namespace="##any"` permits.

**`xs:choice` / `xs:all` / nillable / default/fixed / attributes / namespaces:**
- `xs:choice` (`writeChoice`, lines 173-187): if the choice itself is optional (`minOccurs==0`), it is included ~70% of the time (`OPTIONAL_INCLUDE_PROBABILITY = 0.70`, same constant used for optional elements/attributes). When included, it repeats `repeatCountFor(minOccurs, maxOccurs)` times, and **each repetition independently picks one branch uniformly at random** (`items.get(rnd.nextInt(items.size()))`) — no weighting toward branches already used.
- `xs:all` (lines 149-152): walked identically to `xs:sequence`, i.e. children written in declared order via the same `writeParticleMember`. None of the 4 checked-in XSDs actually declare an `xs:all` (`grep -c "<xs:all"` = 0 in all four), so this path is unexercised by the real schemas.
- **Nillable, `default`, `fixed`**: none of these are read anywhere in the generate code — there is no call to `isNillable()`, `getDefaultValue()`, or `getFixedValue()` in the module (`grep` across `src/main` found zero matches). A required element is always written with a freshly generated value even if the schema declares a `fixed` value for it. (None of the 4 checked-in XSDs use `nillable`, `default=`, or `fixed=` either, so this gap is not exercised by the real schemas, but it is a real gap in the code.)
- Attributes (`writeAttributes`, lines 125-142): required attributes always written; optional attributes included with the same 70% probability; value generated via the same `SimpleTypeResolver`/`ValueGenerator` path as elements.
- Namespaces: a single fixed prefix `"ns"` is bound once on the root element (`writer.writeNamespace(NS_PREFIX, namespace)`, called only when `declareNamespace=true`, i.e. only for the root call in `writeDocument`); every element thereafter is written with `writer.writeStartElement("ns", localName, namespace)` using the schema's single target namespace. Attributes are written unqualified (`writer.writeAttribute(attr.getName(), ...)`, no namespace argument). StAX "repairing namespaces" mode is deliberately not used (code comment, `XmlInstanceGenerator.java:54-58`) specifically so that the same seed produces byte-identical output run to run.

**Streaming vs in-memory.** Real file writes go straight to a file `OutputStream`
(`Files.newOutputStream(outFile)`, `GenerateCommand.java:158`) wrapped in a StAX
`XMLStreamWriter` — the XML is streamed out element-by-element, not built as a DOM or string in
memory first. The only in-memory buffering in the module is during size-tier *calibration*, which
writes a few throwaway trial documents to a capped in-memory `ByteArrayOutputStream`
(`BoundedByteArrayOutputStream`, lines 171-185) purely to measure their size before picking a
repeat factor; those trial documents are discarded, never written to disk.

## 3. Generate mode: real run results

Run as: `java -jar xml-toolkit/target/xml-toolkit.jar generate --xsd <xsd> --out <dir> --count 200 --size mixed --seed 42`
(count reduced from the requested 1000 to 200 per the note at the top of this report).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| seev.035 (seev_035_001_16) | 200 | 200 | not exposed by tool output* | 0 | 67/67/66 | 473.84 s | 0.4 |
| seev.036 (seev_036_001_16) | 200 | 200 | not exposed by tool output* | 0 | 67/67/66 | 377.88 s | 0.5 |
| supl.009 (CAPA_Extension) | 200 | 200 | not exposed by tool output* | 0 | 67/67/66 | 76.02 s | 2.6 |
| supl.011 (CACO_Extension) | 200 | 200 | not exposed by tool output* | 0 | 67/67/66 | 106.35 s | 1.9 |

\* `GenerateResult` only accumulates `validCount`/`invalidCount`/`totalBytes`/`elapsedMillis`
(`GenerateResult.java:10-14`); the per-file retry loop in `GenerateCommand.run` (lines 60-68) does
not record how many of the 1..5 attempts actually succeeded, and nothing is printed for a file that
fails once then succeeds on retry — only a file that **still** fails after all 5 attempts gets a
`[WARN]` line (line 76). So "needed retries" cannot be determined from the tool's own output; it
would require instrumenting the code, which this review does not do.

**Validation errors / failures:** zero. Across all 800 files generated in this run (4 XSDs × 200
files), `invalid=0` in every run and no `[WARN]` lines appeared in any of the four run logs. There
are no validation error messages to report for section 3 — every file validated against its XSD,
either on the first attempt or a retry.

Notable fact from these numbers: the `large` tier targets ~977 KB (`SizeTier.LARGE = 1_000_000`
bytes), but seev.035's large-tier min is 0.98 KB and supl.011's large-tier min is 0.50 KB —
essentially the same size as a `small` file. This matches the behavior documented in the
project's own README ("deeply-nested `xs:choice` schemas can by chance skip whole rich sub-trees"):
seev.035 and supl.011 both have many `xs:choice` points (88 and 8 respectively, see section 1's
element counts), so an unlucky run of choice outcomes can skip most optional content even when the
repeat factor was calibrated for a 1 MB median.

## 4. Infer mode: how it works and real run results

| Responsibility | Class |
|---|---|
| Parse CLI options | `InferOptions` |
| Read every sample XML with StAX, merge into one tree | `XmlStructureScanner` → `ElementNode` |
| Guess a leaf's XSD datatype from its observed text samples | `DatatypeGuesser` |
| Render the merged tree as an XSD | `XsdWriter` |
| Render the plain-language review report | `ReviewReportWriter` |
| Orchestrate: scan → write XSD → write report → validate inputs against the new XSD | `InferCommand` |

**Namespace handling.** `XsdWriter.write()` reads the root element's namespace URI
(`root.qname.getNamespaceURI()`); if non-empty, it emits `targetNamespace="<ns>"` and
`elementFormDefault="qualified"` on the generated `<xs:schema>`, and prefixes every reference to a
generated named type with `tns:` (`XsdWriter.java:25-40`). Confirmed in the real run below — the
inferred schema's header is:
```xml
<xs:schema xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:tns="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:seev.035.001.16" targetNamespace="urn:iso:std:iso:20022:tech:xsd:seev.035.001.16" elementFormDefault="qualified">
```

**Real run: `infer` on 50 generated `seev.035` samples** (the first 50, by filename sort order, of
the 200 valid `seev.035` files from section 3 — i.e. real generator output, not hand-crafted):

```
java -jar xml-toolkit/target/xml-toolkit.jar infer --xml <50-file-dir> --out seev035_inferred.xsd
```

| | Original XSD | Inferred XSD |
|---|---|---|
| Total `<xs:element>` declarations (incl. reused refs) | 227 | 340 |
| Distinct element local names | 65 | 143 |
| `<xs:complexType>` count | 95 | 183 |

(The original reuses a small number of named complexTypes — e.g. shared amount/currency/code
types — across many different parent contexts, so its distinct-name count is much lower than its
tag count. The inferred XSD creates a separate complexType per element position the way `XsdWriter`
walks the tree — it does not detect or merge structurally-identical types that occur under
different parents, so both its tag count and complexType count come out higher than the original
despite describing a smaller observed vocabulary of 143 vs. 65 names.)

**Validation of the 50 samples against the XSD inferred from themselves: 1 / 50 valid (2%).**
49 of 50 failed, all with `cvc-complex-type.2.4.a` ("Invalid content was found starting with
element X, one of Y is expected" — a child-element-order mismatch). This is the direct, observed
consequence of the documented "cannot detect `xs:choice`" gap (next subsection): `seev.035`'s root
content model is built from a long chain of `xs:choice` groups, so different sample files legally
contain the alternatives in different presence/absence combinations. `XsdWriter` has no concept of
choice — it always emits a single `xs:sequence` using the order elements were first encountered
across all 50 samples, with `minOccurs="0"` on anything not present in every sample. Any sample
whose actual (valid, schema-permitted) element order or combination differs from that one
first-seen ordering fails strict sequence validation. Top 5 (by first occurrence) error messages
observed, with the element that triggered each:

| # | Element causing it | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `MvmntPrlimryAdvcId` | `cvc-complex-type.2.4.a: Invalid content was found starting with element '...MvmntPrlimryAdvcId'. One of '...Tp' is expected.` |
| 2 | `Pgntn` | `cvc-complex-type.2.4.a: Invalid content was found starting with element '...Pgntn'. One of '...MvmntPrlimryAdvcGnlInf' is expected.` |
| 3 | `RvslRsn` | `cvc-complex-type.2.4.a: Invalid content was found starting with element '...RvslRsn'. One of '...CorpActnGnlInf' is expected.` |

(Only these 3 distinct messages occurred across the 49 failures — repeated many times each, since
every failing file hits one of these three order mismatches at the very first divergence point in
the document.)

**What infer cannot detect** (from reading `XsdWriter`/`ReviewReportWriter`/`DatatypeGuesser`, and
confirmed empirically by the 1/50 result above):
- `xs:choice` — never modeled; everything is emitted as `xs:sequence`. This is the direct cause of the 49/50 validation failures above.
- `xs:pattern` facets — not inferred at all; leaves fall back to coarse datatype guessing only.
- Length facets (`minLength`/`maxLength`/`length`), `totalDigits`/`fractionDigits`, `min/maxInclusive/Exclusive` — none inferred.
- Enumerations — only **flagged** in the review report as a note ("only X, Y seen → could be an enumeration. Please confirm.") when a leaf has 2–6 distinct observed values across all samples (`ReviewReportWriter.ENUM_MAX_DISTINCT = 6`); never written into the XSD as an actual `xs:enumeration` restriction.
- `xs:all` — never emitted; every complex type uses `xs:sequence`.
- Type reuse/deduplication — every element position gets its own freshly-named complexType (`newTypeName`, `XsdWriter.java:71-75`), even if structurally identical to one used elsewhere; confirmed above (183 inferred complexTypes vs. 95 in the original for the same 65-vs-143-name vocabulary).
- Attribute/element namespaces beyond the single root-level `targetNamespace` — `XmlStructureScanner` does track each element's/attribute's `QName`, but `XsdWriter` only ever uses the root's namespace for `targetNamespace`; nothing attribute-specific (e.g. `attributeFormDefault`) is inferred.
- `nillable`, annotations/documentation — not read from source XMLs (there is nothing to read — plain XML instances don't carry nillable/documentation — and nothing is emitted for them either).

## 6. Known limitations

**Explicit markers in code:** none. `grep -rniE "TODO|FIXME|simplifi|hack|workaround|XXX"` across
all of `xml-toolkit/src` returns zero matches.

**Weak points found by reading the code and/or confirmed by real run output in this report**
(cross-referenced to the section that establishes each fact):

1. `xs:any` is filled with one fixed, hardcoded stub element regardless of the actual extension schema or namespace rules declared by `processContents`/`namespace` (section 2).
2. `nillable`, `default`, and `fixed` facets are never read anywhere in the generate code (section 2) — not exercised by the 4 checked-in XSDs, but a real gap if used against a different schema.
3. The per-file retry mechanism (up to 5 attempts) does not expose, in any printed output, how many files needed a retry versus passed on the first attempt — only final valid/invalid totals and a `[WARN]` for files that exhaust all 5 attempts (section 3).
4. `XsdPatternSampler` does not support regex anchors, backreferences, lookahead/lookbehind, Unicode property escapes, non-greedy quantifiers, or negated shorthand classes `\D`/`\W`/`\S` (silently treated as the literal escaped character) (section 2).
5. Infer mode cannot detect `xs:choice`, which causes a severe, measured drop in round-trip validity: only 1 of 50 real `seev.035` samples validated against the XSD inferred from those same 50 samples (section 4).
6. Infer mode never deduplicates/reuses complexTypes across different parent contexts, so the inferred XSD for `seev.035` has more total element declarations (340 vs. 227) and more complexTypes (183 vs. 95) than the original despite describing fewer distinct element names (143 vs. 65) (section 4).
7. Generate throughput varies substantially by schema: 0.4–0.5 files/sec for `seev.035`/`seev.036` versus 1.9–2.6 files/sec for `supl.009`/`supl.011` at `--size mixed --count 200` on this machine (section 3) — observed only; no profiling was done to attribute this to a specific cause.

@@@=== FILE END ===
@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/generate/ContentLevel.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.generate;

/**
 * How much of the schema's optional content a generated document includes.
 * {@code --size} only has an effect at {@link #FULL} -- the other two levels always write
 * exactly one occurrence of any repeating element, so there's no size tier to calibrate.
 */
public enum ContentLevel {
    /** Required elements/attributes only (minOccurs&gt;=1), one occurrence each. */
    REQUIRED_ONLY(1),
    /** Required and optional, but still one occurrence of anything that repeats. */
    REQUIRED_AND_OPTIONAL(2),
    /** Required, optional, and repetitions -- the original behavior, sized by {@code --size}. */
    FULL(3);

    public final int number;

    ContentLevel(int number) {
        this.number = number;
    }

    public static ContentLevel fromNumber(int n) {
        for (ContentLevel level : values()) {
            if (level.number == n) {
                return level;
            }
        }
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("--level must be 1, 2, or 3, got: " + n);
    }
}

@@@=== FILE END ===
@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/generate/ErrorInjectionContext.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.generate;

/**
 * Drives the two-pass error injection used by {@link XmlInstanceGenerator}: pass 1 runs with
 * {@code targetIndex == -1} purely to count how many points in this specific document are
 * eligible for the chosen error type (eligibility depends on the random structure actually
 * generated, not just what the schema allows in general); pass 2 re-runs with the SAME seed
 * (so it reproduces the identical document up to the injection point) and {@code targetIndex}
 * set to a point chosen from that count, so exactly one occurrence is corrupted and the rest of
 * the document stays exactly as it would have been without injection.
 */
final class ErrorInjectionContext {

    final String errorType;
    final int targetIndex;
    private int seenCount;
    boolean applied;
    String elementPath;
    String originalValue;
    String injectedValue;

    ErrorInjectionContext(String errorType, int targetIndex) {
        this.errorType = errorType;
        this.targetIndex = targetIndex;
    }

    static ErrorInjectionContext countingPass(String errorType) {
        return new ErrorInjectionContext(errorType, -1);
    }

    int eligibleCount() {
        return seenCount;
    }

    boolean isEligible(String type) {
        return errorType.equals(type);
    }

    /** Call once per eligible occurrence found while walking; returns true at most once per
     * document, exactly at the chosen occurrence, and only during the injection pass. */
    boolean shouldInjectThisOccurrence() {
        int index = seenCount++;
        if (applied || targetIndex < 0) {
            return false;
        }
        return index == targetIndex;
    }

    void recordApplied(String elementPath, String originalValue, String injectedValue) {
        this.applied = true;
        this.elementPath = elementPath;
        this.originalValue = originalValue;
        this.injectedValue = injectedValue;
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/generate/ErrorManifestEntry.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.generate;

/** One row of the per-run error-injection manifest (A6/A11): what happened to one generated file. */
public record ErrorManifestEntry(String fileName, boolean isError, String errorType,
                                  String elementPath, String originalValue, String injectedValue) {

    static ErrorManifestEntry valid(String fileName) {
        return new ErrorManifestEntry(fileName, false, null, null, null, null);
    }

    public String toCsvRow() {
        return csv(fileName) + "," + (isError ? "error" : "valid") + "," + csv(errorType) + ","
                + csv(elementPath) + "," + csv(originalValue) + "," + csv(injectedValue);
    }

    private static String csv(String s) {
        if (s == null) {
            return "";
        }
        String escaped = s.replace("\"", "\"\"");
        return "\"" + escaped + "\"";
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/generate/ErrorManifestWriter.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.generate;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;

/** Writes the per-file error-injection manifest (A6/A11) in both CSV and JSON, through the same
 * {@link OutputTarget} every generated file went through (folder, zip, or stream -- A10). */
final class ErrorManifestWriter {

    private ErrorManifestWriter() {
    }

    static void write(List<ErrorManifestEntry> entries, OutputTarget target) throws IOException {
        StringBuilder csv = new StringBuilder("fileName,status,errorType,elementPath,originalValue,injectedValue\n");
        for (ErrorManifestEntry e : entries) {
            csv.append(e.toCsvRow()).append('\n');
        }
        target.write("manifest.csv", csv.toString());

        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("[\n");
        for (int i = 0; i < entries.size(); i++) {
            ErrorManifestEntry e = entries.get(i);
            json.append("  {\"fileName\":").append(q(e.fileName()))
                    .append(",\"status\":").append(q(e.isError() ? "error" : "valid"))
                    .append(",\"errorType\":").append(q(e.errorType()))
                    .append(",\"elementPath\":").append(q(e.elementPath()))
                    .append(",\"originalValue\":").append(q(e.originalValue()))
                    .append(",\"injectedValue\":").append(q(e.injectedValue()))
                    .append('}').append(i == entries.size() - 1 ? "\n" : ",\n");
        }
        json.append("]\n");
        target.write("manifest.json", json.toString());
    }

    private static String q(String s) {
        if (s == null) {
            return "null";
        }
        return "\"" + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\"";
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/generate/FolderOutputTarget.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.generate;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;

/** Writes each file to its own path in a directory -- the original behavior, and still the
 * default. Safe to call concurrently: distinct file names mean distinct file handles. */
final class FolderOutputTarget implements OutputTarget {

    private final Path dir;

    FolderOutputTarget(Path dir) throws IOException {
        this.dir = dir;
        Files.createDirectories(dir);
    }

    @Override
    public void write(String fileName, String content) throws IOException {
        Files.writeString(dir.resolve(fileName), content);
    }

    @Override
    public void close() {
        // Nothing to release; each write already closed its own file handle.
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/generate/GenerateCommand.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.generate;

import com.project.toolkit.validate.XsdValidatorCache;

import javax.xml.stream.XMLOutputFactory;
import javax.xml.stream.XMLStreamWriter;
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.EnumMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Random;

/**
 * Generates N sample XMLs for one XSD: picks a size tier per file, streams it out with StAX,
 * validates it against the XSD, and regenerates (with a different seed) on validation failure.
 */
public final class GenerateCommand {

    private static final int MAX_REGENERATE_ATTEMPTS = 5;
    private static final int MAX_CALIBRATION_ATTEMPTS = 6;
    private static final int CALIBRATION_TRIALS_PER_ATTEMPT = 3;
    private static final long CALIBRATION_TRIAL_HARD_CAP_BYTES = 30_000_000L;
    private static final int MAX_REPEAT_FACTOR = 500;

    public static GenerateResult run(GenerateOptions opts) throws IOException {
        SchemaIndex index = new SchemaIndex(opts.xsd);
        String rootName = index.rootElement.getName();
        ContentLevel level = ContentLevel.fromNumber(opts.level);
        // --size only matters at level 3 (it drives the repeat-factor calibration below); at
        // levels 1-2 every file is exactly "1 occurrence of everything allowed at that level",
        // so there's no tier to plan or calibrate -- one flat, uncalibrated pseudo-tier for
        // bookkeeping (file naming, GenerateResult's per-tier counts) is enough.
        List<SizeTier> plan = level == ContentLevel.FULL
                ? buildSizePlan(opts.size, opts.count)
                : java.util.Collections.nCopies(opts.count, SizeTier.SMALL);
        NameValueProfile profile = opts.profile != null ? NameValueProfile.load(opts.profile) : NameValueProfile.defaultProfile();

        List<String> errorTypes = List.of();
        if (opts.errorPercent > 0) {
            SchemaScanResult scan = SchemaScanner.scan(index);
            errorTypes = opts.errorTypes == null
                    ? List.copyOf(scan.possibleErrorTypes)
                    : opts.errorTypes.stream().filter(scan.possibleErrorTypes::contains).toList();
            if (errorTypes.isEmpty()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("--error-types has none this XSD supports; it supports: " + scan.possibleErrorTypes);
            }
        }
        List<ErrorManifestEntry> manifest = new ArrayList<>();

        SchemaIndex supplementIndex = opts.supplement != null ? new SchemaIndex(opts.supplement) : null;

        // Namespace prefix/declaration is written explicitly by XmlInstanceGenerator (fixed
        // prefix, declared once on the root), so repairing namespaces is deliberately left off --
        // its auto-prefix counter isn't seeded and would break "same seed -> same output".
        XMLOutputFactory outputFactory = XMLOutputFactory.newInstance();

        // Calibrate once per distinct size tier in this run: the repeat factor needed to hit a
        // tier's target byte size is driven by the XSD's nesting shape, not by file content, so
        // one calibration per (xsd, tier) is reused across every file of that tier.
        Map<SizeTier, Integer> repeatFactorByTier = new EnumMap<>(SizeTier.class);
        if (level == ContentLevel.FULL) {
            for (SizeTier tier : distinctTiers(plan)) {
                repeatFactorByTier.put(tier, calibrateRepeatFactor(index, tier, outputFactory, opts.seed, profile));
            }
        } else {
            repeatFactorByTier.put(SizeTier.SMALL, 1);
        }

        GenerateResult result = new GenerateResult();
        result.totalRequested = opts.count;
        long start = System.currentTimeMillis();

        try (OutputTarget target = openOutputTarget(opts)) {
            // Each file is fully independent (its own seed, own output path, own retry loop), so
            // the per-file work submits to a thread pool -- "each thread with its own writer" is
            // already true of every task below, since each one creates its own XMLStreamWriter
            // rather than sharing one; only the final GenerateResult/manifest merge (not the file
            // generation itself) needs to happen back on this thread, to avoid synchronizing shared
            // mutable state across workers. The OutputTarget itself (folder or zip) is shared, but
            // each implementation documents how it stays safe under concurrent writes.
            List<FileOutcome> outcomes;
            java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService pool = java.util.concurrent.Executors.newFixedThreadPool(opts.threads);
            try {
                List<String> finalErrorTypes = errorTypes;
                java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger completed = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger();
                List<java.util.concurrent.Future<FileOutcome>> futures = new ArrayList<>(plan.size());
                for (int i = 0; i < plan.size(); i++) {
                    if (opts.cancelled != null && opts.cancelled.getAsBoolean()) {
                        break;
                    }
                    final int fileIndex = i;
                    futures.add(pool.submit(() -> {
                        FileOutcome outcome = processOneFile(index, rootName, plan.get(fileIndex), repeatFactorByTier,
                                opts, profile, level, finalErrorTypes, supplementIndex, fileIndex, target);
                        // Reported from whichever worker finishes, as soon as it finishes -- real
                        // progress, not submission order -- so a caller tracking job % sees it
                        // move as work actually completes rather than only at the very end.
                        if (opts.onFileDone != null) {
                            opts.onFileDone.accept(completed.incrementAndGet());
                        }
                        return outcome;
                    }));
                }
                outcomes = new ArrayList<>(futures.size());
                for (var future : futures) {
                    outcomes.add(future.get());
                }
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {
                Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
                throw new IOException("Generation interrupted", e);
            } catch (java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException e) {
                throw new IOException("Failed generating a file: " + e.getCause().getMessage(), e.getCause());
            } finally {
                pool.shutdown();
            }

            for (FileOutcome outcome : outcomes) {
                manifest.add(outcome.manifestEntry());
                if (outcome.failedAfterRetries()) {
                    result.invalidCount++;
                    System.err.println("  [WARN] " + outcome.manifestEntry().fileName() + " failed validation after "
                            + MAX_REGENERATE_ATTEMPTS + " attempts: " + outcome.lastReason());
                    continue;
                }
                if (outcome.manifestEntry().isError()) {
                    result.errorCountByType.merge(outcome.manifestEntry().errorType(), 1, Integer::sum);
                } else {
                    result.validCount++;
                }
                result.countPerTier.merge(outcome.tier(), 1, Integer::sum);
                result.noteFileSize(outcome.bytes());
            }

            result.elapsedMillis = System.currentTimeMillis() - start;
            // Written for every run, not just error-injection ones: a plain valid run is still
            // "N files, M bytes, T seconds" worth reporting, and the per-file manifest is what
            // makes report.json/csv's aggregate counts independently checkable (A11). In zip mode
            // these go beside the zip as loose files rather than inside it, so the artifact a
            // caller downloads is XML documents only -- reporting still happens every run, just
            // not bundled into that particular file. Folder mode already writes them as loose
            // files in the output folder (nothing to change); stream mode has no secondary
            // location to put them in, so they stay bundled in the one stream that exists.
            OutputTarget reportsTarget = "zip".equals(opts.output)
                    ? new FolderOutputTarget(opts.out.getParent() != null ? opts.out.getParent() : Path.of("."))
                    : target;
            try {
                ErrorManifestWriter.write(manifest, reportsTarget);
                GenerateReportWriter.write(opts, result, reportsTarget);
            } finally {
                if (reportsTarget != target) {
                    reportsTarget.close();
                }
            }
        }

        return result;
    }

    private static OutputTarget openOutputTarget(GenerateOptions opts) throws IOException {
        return switch (opts.output) {
            case "folder" -> new FolderOutputTarget(opts.out);
            case "zip" -> {
                if (opts.out.getParent() != null) {
                    Files.createDirectories(opts.out.getParent());
                }
                yield new ZipOutputTarget(Files.newOutputStream(opts.out));
            }
            case "stream" -> new ZipOutputTarget(opts.streamTarget != null ? opts.streamTarget : System.out);
            default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown --output: " + opts.output);
        };
    }

    private record FileOutcome(ErrorManifestEntry manifestEntry, SizeTier tier, long bytes,
                                boolean failedAfterRetries, String lastReason) {
    }

    private static FileOutcome processOneFile(SchemaIndex index, String rootName, SizeTier tier,
                                               Map<SizeTier, Integer> repeatFactorByTier, GenerateOptions opts,
                                               NameValueProfile profile, ContentLevel level, List<String> errorTypes,
                                               SchemaIndex supplementIndex, int fileIndex, OutputTarget target) throws IOException {
        // Each task gets its own factory: StAX writer instances must not be shared across
        // threads, and a factory is cheap enough that creating one per file removes any doubt.
        XMLOutputFactory outputFactory = XMLOutputFactory.newInstance();
        int repeatFactor = repeatFactorByTier.get(tier);
        String fileName = rootName + "_" + tier.label() + "_" + (fileIndex + 1) + ".xml";
        boolean embedSupplement = supplementIndex != null;

        long baseFileSeed = opts.seed + (long) fileIndex * 7919L;
        boolean wantsError = !errorTypes.isEmpty()
                && new Random(baseFileSeed ^ 0xE4404L).nextInt(100) < opts.errorPercent;

        if (wantsError) {
            String chosenType = errorTypes.get(new Random(baseFileSeed ^ 0xC0DE1L).nextInt(errorTypes.size()));
            InjectionOutcome injected = injectOne(index, repeatFactor, baseFileSeed, outputFactory, fileName, target,
                    profile, level, chosenType, opts.xsd, supplementIndex, opts.supplement);
            return new FileOutcome(injected.entry(), tier, injected.bytes(), false, null);
        }

        boolean valid = false;
        String lastReason = null;
        String xml = null;
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_REGENERATE_ATTEMPTS && !valid; attempt++) {
            long fileSeed = baseFileSeed + attempt * 104_729L;
            xml = generateToString(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, profile, level, null, embedSupplement);
            if (embedSupplement) {
                xml = embedSupplements(xml, supplementIndex, opts.supplement, fileSeed ^ 0xABCDEFL);
            }
            var check = XsdValidatorCache.validateString(opts.xsd, xml);
            valid = check.valid();
            lastReason = check.reason();
        }
        target.write(fileName, xml);

        if (valid) {
            return new FileOutcome(ErrorManifestEntry.valid(fileName), tier, utf8Length(xml), false, null);
        }
        return new FileOutcome(ErrorManifestEntry.valid(fileName), tier, 0, true, lastReason);
    }

    private static long utf8Length(String s) {
        return s.getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length;
    }

    private record InjectionOutcome(ErrorManifestEntry entry, long bytes) {
    }

    /** Generates one file with exactly one deliberate error of {@code errorType} and confirms it
     * now fails validation for that reason, per A6. Falls back to "invalid-characters" (a plain
     * post-serialization text edit that always applies to any non-empty document) whenever the
     * requested type turns out to have no eligible occurrence in this specific random document,
     * or -- as a last-resort safety net -- whenever the injected document unexpectedly still
     * validates. */
    private static InjectionOutcome injectOne(SchemaIndex index, int repeatFactor, long fileSeed,
                                               XMLOutputFactory outputFactory, String fileName, OutputTarget target,
                                               NameValueProfile profile, ContentLevel level, String errorType, Path xsdPath,
                                               SchemaIndex supplementIndex, Path supplementXsd) throws IOException {
        boolean embedSupplement = supplementIndex != null;
        if ("malformed-xml".equals(errorType)) {
            String valid = generateToString(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, profile, level, null, embedSupplement);
            if (embedSupplement) {
                valid = embedSupplements(valid, supplementIndex, supplementXsd, fileSeed ^ 0xABCDEFL);
            }
            String corrupted = removeLastClosingTag(valid);
            target.write(fileName, corrupted);
            boolean failedAsExpected = !XsdValidatorCache.validateString(xsdPath, corrupted).valid();
            return new InjectionOutcome(new ErrorManifestEntry(fileName, failedAsExpected, "malformed-xml",
                    "(end of document)", "(well-formed XML)", "(root closing tag removed)"), utf8Length(corrupted));
        }
        if ("invalid-characters".equals(errorType)) {
            return applyInvalidCharacters(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, fileName, target, profile, level,
                    xsdPath, supplementIndex, supplementXsd);
        }

        ErrorInjectionContext counting = ErrorInjectionContext.countingPass(errorType);
        generateToString(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, profile, level, counting, embedSupplement);
        if (counting.eligibleCount() == 0) {
            // This document's random structure doesn't happen to contain anything eligible for
            // errorType (e.g. no enum-valued field ended up present) even though the schema
            // supports it in general -- fall back to the always-applicable type.
            return applyInvalidCharacters(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, fileName, target, profile, level,
                    xsdPath, supplementIndex, supplementXsd);
        }

        Random decisionRnd = new Random(fileSeed ^ 0xC0DE2L);
        ErrorInjectionContext inject = new ErrorInjectionContext(errorType, decisionRnd.nextInt(counting.eligibleCount()));
        String xml = generateToString(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, profile, level, inject, embedSupplement);
        if (embedSupplement) {
            xml = embedSupplements(xml, supplementIndex, supplementXsd, fileSeed ^ 0xABCDEFL);
        }
        if (XsdValidatorCache.validateString(xsdPath, xml).valid()) {
            // Safety net: shouldn't happen given how each type is constructed, but confirm --
            // don't claim a file is a validation-failing error example when it isn't one.
            return applyInvalidCharacters(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, fileName, target, profile, level,
                    xsdPath, supplementIndex, supplementXsd);
        }
        target.write(fileName, xml);
        return new InjectionOutcome(new ErrorManifestEntry(fileName, true, errorType,
                inject.elementPath, inject.originalValue, inject.injectedValue), utf8Length(xml));
    }

    private static InjectionOutcome applyInvalidCharacters(SchemaIndex index, int repeatFactor, long fileSeed,
                                                             XMLOutputFactory outputFactory, String fileName, OutputTarget target,
                                                             NameValueProfile profile, ContentLevel level,
                                                             Path xsdPath, SchemaIndex supplementIndex,
                                                             Path supplementXsd) throws IOException {
        boolean embedSupplement = supplementIndex != null;
        String valid = generateToString(index, repeatFactor, fileSeed, outputFactory, profile, level, null, embedSupplement);
        if (embedSupplement) {
            valid = embedSupplements(valid, supplementIndex, supplementXsd, fileSeed ^ 0xABCDEFL);
        }
        String[] result = insertIllegalCharacter(valid);
        target.write(fileName, result[0]);
        boolean failedAsExpected = !XsdValidatorCache.validateString(xsdPath, result[0]).valid();
        return new InjectionOutcome(new ErrorManifestEntry(fileName, failedAsExpected, "invalid-characters",
                result[1], result[2], result[3]), utf8Length(result[0]));
    }

    /** Replaces every {@code <SupplementPlaceholder idx="N">} marker (written by
     * {@link XmlInstanceGenerator} when supplement embedding is on) with a freshly generated,
     * independently-validated document from {@code supplementXsd} -- A7's "validate the supl
     * part against its own XSD too", done before it's ever spliced into the outer document. */
    private static String embedSupplements(String xml, SchemaIndex supplementIndex, Path supplementXsd, long seed) throws IOException {
        // Matches both the self-closing form a StAX writer may choose for an empty element
        // (Woodstox) and the explicit open/close form (the JDK's default writer) -- which one
        // appears is an implementation detail of whatever StAX provider is on the classpath.
        java.util.regex.Pattern placeholder = java.util.regex.Pattern.compile(
                "<SupplementPlaceholder idx=\"(\\d+)\"/>|<SupplementPlaceholder idx=\"(\\d+)\"></SupplementPlaceholder>");
        java.util.regex.Matcher m = placeholder.matcher(xml);
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        int last = 0;
        int occurrence = 0;
        while (m.find()) {
            sb.append(xml, last, m.start());
            sb.append(generateValidSupplementFragment(supplementIndex, supplementXsd, seed + occurrence * 999_331L));
            last = m.end();
            occurrence++;
        }
        sb.append(xml.substring(last));
        return sb.toString();
    }

    private static String generateValidSupplementFragment(SchemaIndex supplementIndex, Path supplementXsd, long seed) throws IOException {
        XMLOutputFactory factory = XMLOutputFactory.newInstance();
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_REGENERATE_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
            long trySeed = seed + attempt * 104_729L;
            String full = generateToString(supplementIndex, 1, trySeed, factory, NameValueProfile.defaultProfile(), ContentLevel.FULL, null, false);
            if (XsdValidatorCache.validateString(supplementXsd, full).valid()) {
                return full.replaceFirst("^<\\?xml[^>]*\\?>", "");
            }
        }
        throw new IOException("Could not generate a valid supplement document against " + supplementXsd
                + " after " + MAX_REGENERATE_ATTEMPTS + " attempts");
    }

    /** Removes the document's final closing tag (always the root's, since it's written last),
     * leaving an unclosed element -- guaranteed not well-formed. */
    private static String removeLastClosingTag(String xml) {
        int closeStart = xml.lastIndexOf("</");
        if (closeStart < 0) {
            return xml + "<";
        }
        int closeEnd = xml.indexOf('>', closeStart);
        return closeEnd < 0 ? xml.substring(0, closeStart) : xml.substring(0, closeStart) + xml.substring(closeEnd + 1);
    }

    /** Splices a raw XML 1.0-disallowed control character (U+0001) into the middle of the first
     * non-blank text node found -- verified to survive serialization (unlike writing it through
     * the StAX API, which silently strips it) and to be rejected by the XML parser on reload. */
    private static String[] insertIllegalCharacter(String xml) {
        java.util.regex.Matcher m = java.util.regex.Pattern.compile(">([^<]+)<").matcher(xml);
        while (m.find()) {
            String text = m.group(1);
            if (text.isBlank()) {
                continue;
            }
            int mid = text.length() / 2;
            int insertAt = m.start(1) + mid;
            String corrupted = xml.substring(0, insertAt) + '\u0001' + xml.substring(insertAt);
            String injectedText = text.substring(0, mid) + '\u0001' + text.substring(mid);
            return new String[]{corrupted, "(a text value)", text, injectedText};
        }
        int firstClose = xml.indexOf('>');
        return new String[]{xml.substring(0, firstClose + 1) + '\u0001' + xml.substring(firstClose + 1),
                "(document start)", "", "\u0001"};
    }

    private static String generateToString(SchemaIndex index, int repeatFactor, long seed, XMLOutputFactory outputFactory,
                                            NameValueProfile profile, ContentLevel level, ErrorInjectionContext injection,
                                            boolean embedSupplementPlaceholder) throws IOException {
        try {
            Random rnd = new Random(seed);
            XmlInstanceGenerator generator = new XmlInstanceGenerator(index, repeatFactor, rnd, profile, level, injection, embedSupplementPlaceholder);
            ByteArrayOutputStream bos = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
            XMLStreamWriter writer = new IndentingXmlStreamWriter(outputFactory.createXMLStreamWriter(bos, "UTF-8"));
            generator.writeDocument(writer);
            writer.flush();
            writer.close();
            return bos.toString(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new IOException("Failed generating in-memory XML: " + e.getMessage(), e);
        }
    }

    private static List<SizeTier> distinctTiers(List<SizeTier> plan) {
        List<SizeTier> distinct = new ArrayList<>();
        for (SizeTier tier : plan) {
            if (!distinct.contains(tier)) {
                distinct.add(tier);
            }
        }
        return distinct;
    }

    /**
     * Finds a repeat factor that gets this tier's output within 2x of its target byte size,
     * by generating a few throwaway trials and correcting the factor with a damped power-law
     * step (sqrt of the size ratio) each time. Nested maxOccurs-unbounded lists compound
     * multiplicatively, so a couple of corrections is normally enough; a hard byte cap on each
     * trial keeps a bad guess from blowing up memory while calibrating "large".
     */
    private static int calibrateRepeatFactor(SchemaIndex index, SizeTier tier,
                                              XMLOutputFactory outputFactory, long seed, NameValueProfile profile) {
        if (tier == SizeTier.SMALL) {
            return tier.initialRepeatFactor;
        }
        int factor = tier.initialRepeatFactor;
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < MAX_CALIBRATION_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
            long size = medianTrialSize(index, factor, seed, outputFactory, attempt, profile);
            double ratio = (double) tier.targetBytes / Math.max(1, size);
            if (ratio >= 0.5 && ratio <= 2.0) {
                break;
            }
            int next = (int) Math.round(factor * Math.sqrt(ratio));
            next = Math.max(1, Math.min(next, factor * 4));
            next = Math.min(next, MAX_REPEAT_FACTOR);
            if (next == factor) {
                break;
            }
            factor = next;
        }
        return factor;
    }

    /** Several schema-random trials at the same factor, since optional/choice content can swing
     * a single trial's size a lot; the median is a much more stable signal to calibrate against. */
    private static long medianTrialSize(SchemaIndex index, int factor, long seed,
                                         XMLOutputFactory outputFactory, int attempt, NameValueProfile profile) {
        long[] sizes = new long[CALIBRATION_TRIALS_PER_ATTEMPT];
        for (int t = 0; t < sizes.length; t++) {
            sizes[t] = trialSize(index, factor, seed + attempt * 97L + t * 31L, outputFactory, profile);
        }
        java.util.Arrays.sort(sizes);
        return sizes[sizes.length / 2];
    }

    private static long trialSize(SchemaIndex index, int factor, long seed, XMLOutputFactory outputFactory, NameValueProfile profile) {
        try {
            Random rnd = new Random(seed ^ 0x5EEDL);
            // Calibration only ever runs for the FULL level (see run()), so the trial itself
            // always generates at FULL.
            XmlInstanceGenerator generator = new XmlInstanceGenerator(index, factor, rnd, profile, ContentLevel.FULL, null, false);
            BoundedByteArrayOutputStream bos = new BoundedByteArrayOutputStream(CALIBRATION_TRIAL_HARD_CAP_BYTES);
            XMLStreamWriter writer = outputFactory.createXMLStreamWriter(bos, "UTF-8");
            generator.writeDocument(writer);
            writer.flush();
            writer.close();
            return bos.size();
        } catch (TooBigException e) {
            return CALIBRATION_TRIAL_HARD_CAP_BYTES * 10; // signal "way too big" to force a strong downward correction
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return 1; // unreadable trial: signal "way too small" so calibration grows and tries again
        }
    }

    private static final class TooBigException extends RuntimeException {
    }

    private static final class BoundedByteArrayOutputStream extends ByteArrayOutputStream {
        private final long cap;

        BoundedByteArrayOutputStream(long cap) {
            this.cap = cap;
        }

        @Override
        public synchronized void write(byte[] b, int off, int len) {
            if (size() + len > cap) {
                throw new TooBigException();
            }
            super.write(b, off, len);
        }
    }

    /** Mixed mode cycles small/medium/large roughly one third each, in a fixed repeating order. */
    private static List<SizeTier> buildSizePlan(String size, int count) {
        List<SizeTier> plan = new ArrayList<>(count);
        if (!"mixed".equals(size)) {
            SizeTier tier = SizeTier.valueOf(size.toUpperCase());
            for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
                plan.add(tier);
            }
            return plan;
        }
        SizeTier[] cycle = {SizeTier.SMALL, SizeTier.MEDIUM, SizeTier.LARGE};
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            plan.add(cycle[i % cycle.length]);
        }
        return plan;
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/generate/GenerateOptions.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.generate;

import java.nio.file.Path;

public final class GenerateOptions {
    private static final java.util.List<String> ALLOWED_SIZES = java.util.List.of("small", "medium", "large", "mixed");
    private static final java.util.List<String> ALLOWED_OUTPUTS = java.util.List.of("folder", "zip", "stream");

    public Path xsd;
    public Path out;
    public int count = 1000;
    public String size = "mixed"; // small | medium | large | mixed
    public long seed = System.nanoTime();
    public boolean seedExplicit = false;
    public Path profile;
    public int level = 3;
    public int errorPercent = 0;
    public java.util.List<String> errorTypes; // null = every type the XSD supports
    public Path supplement; // optional: another XSD to generate a valid document for and embed in each xs:any slot
    public int threads = Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors();
    /** folder (default, --out is a directory) | zip (--out is the archive file to create) |
     * stream (writes a ZIP byte stream to {@link #streamTarget}, or stdout if that's null --
     * for a programmatic caller, e.g. a future API response body; A10). */
    public String output = "folder";
    public java.io.OutputStream streamTarget;
    /** Optional: called with the number of files completed so far, each time one finishes --
     * for a caller (the API module's job tracker) that needs incremental progress rather than
     * just the final GenerateResult. Never called concurrently; invoked from the merge loop
     * after all per-file work has already happened in parallel. */
    public java.util.function.IntConsumer onFileDone;
    /** Optional: polled before queuing each new file's work. Once it returns true, no further
     * files are submitted -- already-running ones still finish (best-effort cancellation, the
     * same semantics most job systems give a "cancel" button). Null means never cancelled. */
    public java.util.function.BooleanSupplier cancelled;

    public static GenerateOptions parse(String[] args) {
        GenerateOptions opts = new GenerateOptions();
        for (int i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
            String arg = args[i];
            switch (arg) {
                case "--xsd" -> opts.xsd = Path.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--xsd"));
                case "--out" -> opts.out = Path.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--out"));
                case "--count" -> opts.count = Integer.parseInt(requireValue(args, ++i, "--count"));
                case "--size" -> opts.size = requireValue(args, ++i, "--size");
                case "--seed" -> {
                    opts.seed = Long.parseLong(requireValue(args, ++i, "--seed"));
                    opts.seedExplicit = true;
                }
                case "--profile" -> opts.profile = Path.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--profile"));
                case "--level" -> opts.level = Integer.parseInt(requireValue(args, ++i, "--level"));
                case "--error-percent" -> opts.errorPercent = Integer.parseInt(requireValue(args, ++i, "--error-percent"));
                case "--error-types" -> opts.errorTypes = java.util.List.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--error-types").split(","));
                case "--supplement" -> opts.supplement = Path.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--supplement"));
                case "--threads" -> opts.threads = Integer.parseInt(requireValue(args, ++i, "--threads"));
                case "--output" -> opts.output = requireValue(args, ++i, "--output");
                default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown option: " + arg);
            }
        }
        ContentLevel.fromNumber(opts.level); // validates range eagerly
        if (opts.errorPercent < 0 || opts.errorPercent > 100) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--error-percent must be between 0 and 100, got: " + opts.errorPercent);
        }
        if (opts.threads < 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--threads must be at least 1, got: " + opts.threads);
        }
        if (opts.xsd == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--xsd is required");
        }
        if (!ALLOWED_OUTPUTS.contains(opts.output)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--output must be one of folder|zip|stream, got: " + opts.output);
        }
        // "stream" writes to an OutputStream (stdout by default), not a path on disk, so --out
        // names nothing in that mode.
        if (opts.out == null && !"stream".equals(opts.output)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--out is required");
        }
        if (!java.nio.file.Files.isRegularFile(opts.xsd)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("XSD file not found: " + opts.xsd);
        }
        if (!ALLOWED_SIZES.contains(opts.size)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--size must be one of small|medium|large|mixed, got: " + opts.size);
        }
        return opts;
    }

    private static String requireValue(String[] args, int index, String flag) {
        if (index >= args.length) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(flag + " requires a value");
        }
        return args[index];
    }
}

package com.project.toolkit.generate;

import java.io.IOException;

/** Writes the full per-run report (A11): settings, seed, counts, size stats, time and
 * files/second, in both JSON and CSV, through the same {@link OutputTarget} as the generated
 * files themselves. The per-file manifest (A6) is a separate pair of files written alongside it. */
final class GenerateReportWriter {

    private GenerateReportWriter() {
    }

    static void write(GenerateOptions opts, GenerateResult result, OutputTarget target) throws IOException {
        target.write("report.json", toJson(opts, result));
        target.write("report.csv", toCsv(opts, result));
    }

    private static String toJson(GenerateOptions opts, GenerateResult result) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        sb.append("{\n  \"settings\":{\n")
                .append("    \"xsd\":").append(q(String.valueOf(opts.xsd))).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"out\":").append(q(opts.out == null ? null : String.valueOf(opts.out))).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"output\":").append(q(opts.output)).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"count\":").append(opts.count).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"size\":").append(q(opts.size)).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"level\":").append(opts.level).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"threads\":").append(opts.threads).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"errorPercent\":").append(opts.errorPercent).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"errorTypes\":").append(opts.errorTypes == null ? "null" : listJson(opts.errorTypes)).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"supplement\":").append(q(opts.supplement == null ? null : String.valueOf(opts.supplement))).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"profile\":").append(q(opts.profile == null ? null : String.valueOf(opts.profile))).append('\n')
                .append("  },\n")
                .append("  \"seed\":").append(opts.seed).append(",\n")
                .append("  \"counts\":{\n")
                .append("    \"totalRequested\":").append(result.totalRequested).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"valid\":").append(result.validCount).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"invalid\":").append(result.invalidCount).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"errorByType\":").append(mapJson(result.errorCountByType)).append('\n')
                .append("  },\n")
                .append("  \"sizeBytes\":{\n")
                .append("    \"min\":").append(result.writtenCount() == 0 ? 0 : result.minBytes).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"avg\":").append(String.format("%.1f", result.avgBytes())).append(",\n")
                .append("    \"max\":").append(result.maxBytes).append('\n')
                .append("  },\n")
                .append("  \"timeSeconds\":").append(String.format("%.3f", result.elapsedMillis / 1000.0)).append(",\n")
                .append("  \"filesPerSecond\":").append(String.format("%.2f", result.xmlsPerSecond())).append('\n')
                .append("}\n");
        return sb.toString();
    }

    private static String toCsv(GenerateOptions opts, GenerateResult result) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("key,value\n");
        sb.append("xsd,").append(csv(String.valueOf(opts.xsd))).append('\n');
        sb.append("out,").append(csv(opts.out == null ? "" : String.valueOf(opts.out))).append('\n');
        sb.append("output,").append(csv(opts.output)).append('\n');
        sb.append("count,").append(opts.count).append('\n');
        sb.append("size,").append(csv(opts.size)).append('\n');
        sb.append("level,").append(opts.level).append('\n');
        sb.append("threads,").append(opts.threads).append('\n');
        sb.append("seed,").append(opts.seed).append('\n');
        sb.append("errorPercent,").append(opts.errorPercent).append('\n');
        sb.append("errorTypes,").append(csv(opts.errorTypes == null ? "" : String.join(";", opts.errorTypes))).append('\n');
        sb.append("supplement,").append(csv(opts.supplement == null ? "" : String.valueOf(opts.supplement))).append('\n');
        sb.append("totalRequested,").append(result.totalRequested).append('\n');
        sb.append("valid,").append(result.validCount).append('\n');
        sb.append("invalid,").append(result.invalidCount).append('\n');
        for (var e : result.errorCountByType.entrySet()) {
            sb.append("error.").append(e.getKey()).append(',').append(e.getValue()).append('\n');
        }
        sb.append("minSizeBytes,").append(result.writtenCount() == 0 ? 0 : result.minBytes).append('\n');
        sb.append("avgSizeBytes,").append(String.format("%.1f", result.avgBytes())).append('\n');
        sb.append("maxSizeBytes,").append(result.maxBytes).append('\n');
        sb.append("timeSeconds,").append(String.format("%.3f", result.elapsedMillis / 1000.0)).append('\n');
        sb.append("filesPerSecond,").append(String.format("%.2f", result.xmlsPerSecond())).append('\n');
        return sb.toString();
    }

    private static String listJson(java.util.List<String> values) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("[");
        for (int i = 0; i < values.size(); i++) {
            sb.append(i == 0 ? "" : ",").append(q(values.get(i)));
        }
        return sb.append(']').toString();
    }

    private static String mapJson(java.util.Map<String, Integer> map) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("{");
        int i = 0;
        for (var e : map.entrySet()) {
            sb.append(i++ == 0 ? "" : ",").append(q(e.getKey())).append(':').append(e.getValue());
        }
        return sb.append('}').toString();
    }

    private static String q(String s) {
        if (s == null) {
            return "null";
        }
        return "\"" + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"") + "\"";
    }

    private static String csv(String s) {
        return "\"" + s.replace("\"", "\"\"") + "\"";
    }
}
