package com.project.toolkit.generate;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.zip.ZipEntry;
import java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream;

/** Writes every file as one entry in a ZIP archive, backed by whatever {@link OutputStream} the
 * caller gives it -- a file on disk for {@code --output zip}, or any other stream (a pipe, an
 * HTTP response body) for {@code --output stream}, which is the "same code serves files and
 * streaming" A10 asks for: both paths are this exact class, differing only in which stream backs
 * them. A single underlying {@link ZipOutputStream} isn't safe for concurrent entries, so writes
 * here are serialized -- generation itself still happens in parallel; only this final, comparatively
 * fast I/O step is single-threaded. */
final class ZipOutputTarget implements OutputTarget {

    private final ZipOutputStream zip;

    ZipOutputTarget(OutputStream out) {
        this.zip = new ZipOutputStream(out);
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized void write(String fileName, String content) throws IOException {
        zip.putNextEntry(new ZipEntry(fileName));
        zip.write(content.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        zip.closeEntry();
    }

    @Override
    public void close() throws IOException {
        zip.close();
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/BaselineDiff.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import org.apache.ws.commons.schema.*;

import java.io.FileInputStream;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Diffs the freshly-inferred tree against a previously-written XSD (typically one this tool
 * wrote on an earlier run), reporting only what changed. Only understands the shape this tool's
 * own {@link XsdWriter} produces (named complexTypes, each a flat xs:sequence of elements/
 * xs:choice, or xs:simpleContent) -- a hand-written XSD with imports/groups/xs:all is out of
 * scope for this best-effort comparison.
 */
final class BaselineDiff {

    record FieldInfo(String type, boolean required, boolean repeats) {
    }

    record Change(String path, String kind, String before, String after) {
    }

    private BaselineDiff() {
    }

    static java.util.List<Change> diff(ElementNode newRoot, Path baselineXsd) {
        Map<String, FieldInfo> before = flattenBaseline(baselineXsd);
        Map<String, FieldInfo> after = flattenNew(newRoot, "", 0, true);

        java.util.List<Change> changes = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
        for (var entry : after.entrySet()) {
            FieldInfo oldInfo = before.get(entry.getKey());
            if (oldInfo == null) {
                changes.add(new Change(entry.getKey(), "added", "-", describe(entry.getValue())));
                continue;
            }
            FieldInfo newInfo = entry.getValue();
            if (oldInfo.required() != newInfo.required()) {
                changes.add(new Change(entry.getKey(), "requiredness changed",
                        oldInfo.required() ? "required" : "optional", newInfo.required() ? "required" : "optional"));
            }
            if (!oldInfo.type().equals(newInfo.type())) {
                changes.add(new Change(entry.getKey(), "datatype changed", oldInfo.type(), newInfo.type()));
            }
            if (oldInfo.repeats() != newInfo.repeats()) {
                changes.add(new Change(entry.getKey(), "repeats changed", String.valueOf(oldInfo.repeats()), String.valueOf(newInfo.repeats())));
            }
        }
        for (String path : before.keySet()) {
            if (!after.containsKey(path)) {
                changes.add(new Change(path, "removed", describe(before.get(path)), "-"));
            }
        }
        return changes;
    }

    private static String describe(FieldInfo info) {
        return info.type() + (info.required() ? " (required)" : " (optional)") + (info.repeats() ? " (repeats)" : "");
    }

    private static Map<String, FieldInfo> flattenNew(ElementNode node, String path, int parentTotalInstances, boolean isRoot) {
        Map<String, FieldInfo> out = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        String name = path.isEmpty() ? node.qname.getLocalPart() : path + "/" + node.qname.getLocalPart();
        String type = node.hasChildren ? "complex" : DatatypeGuesser.guess(node.textSamples, node.qname.getLocalPart());
        boolean required = isRoot || node.isRequired(parentTotalInstances);
        out.put(name, new FieldInfo(type, required, node.repeats()));
        for (ElementNode child : node.children.values()) {
            out.putAll(flattenNew(child, name, node.totalInstances, false));
        }
        return out;
    }

    private static Map<String, FieldInfo> flattenBaseline(Path baselineXsd) {
        Map<String, FieldInfo> out = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        XmlSchemaCollection collection = new XmlSchemaCollection();
        XmlSchema schema;
        try (InputStream in = new FileInputStream(baselineXsd.toFile())) {
            schema = collection.read(new org.xml.sax.InputSource(in));
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Could not parse baseline XSD: " + baselineXsd + " -- " + e.getMessage(), e);
        }
        if (schema.getElements().isEmpty()) {
            return out;
        }
        XmlSchemaElement root = schema.getElements().values().iterator().next();
        walkBaseline(collection, root, "", out, true);
        return out;
    }

    private static void walkBaseline(XmlSchemaCollection collection, XmlSchemaElement element, String path,
                                      Map<String, FieldInfo> out, boolean isRoot) {
        String name = path.isEmpty() ? element.getName() : path + "/" + element.getName();
        boolean required = isRoot || element.getMinOccurs() >= 1;
        boolean repeats = element.getMaxOccurs() > 1;

        XmlSchemaType type = element.getSchemaType();
        if (type == null && element.getSchemaTypeName() != null) {
            type = collection.getTypeByQName(element.getSchemaTypeName());
        }
        if (type instanceof XmlSchemaComplexType complexType) {
            out.put(name, new FieldInfo("complex", required, repeats));
            if (complexType.getParticle() instanceof XmlSchemaSequence seq) {
                for (XmlSchemaSequenceMember member : seq.getItems()) {
                    walkBaselineMember(collection, member, name, out);
                }
            } else if (complexType.getContentModel() instanceof XmlSchemaSimpleContent) {
                // Leaf with attributes only; already recorded as "complex" above -- good enough
                // for this diff's purposes (attribute-level diffing is out of scope).
            }
        } else {
            String typeName = element.getSchemaTypeName() != null ? element.getSchemaTypeName().getLocalPart() : "string";
            out.put(name, new FieldInfo(typeName, required, repeats));
        }
    }

    private static void walkBaselineMember(XmlSchemaCollection collection, Object member, String path, Map<String, FieldInfo> out) {
        if (member instanceof XmlSchemaElement el) {
            walkBaseline(collection, el, path, out, false);
        } else if (member instanceof XmlSchemaChoice choice) {
            for (Object item : choice.getItems()) {
                walkBaselineMember(collection, item, path, out);
            }
        }
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/ChoiceGrouper.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import javax.xml.namespace.QName;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Detects xs:choice among a node's direct children: a set of siblings that never co-occur in
 * the same parent occurrence but, together, cover every occurrence (or every occurrence where
 * at least one of them is present). Children not part of any such group are left as plain
 * sequence members, unchanged from the original required/optional logic.
 */
final class ChoiceGrouper {

    sealed interface Slot permits SingleSlot, ChoiceSlot {
    }

    record SingleSlot(ElementNode child) implements Slot {
    }

    record ChoiceSlot(List<ElementNode> members, boolean required) implements Slot {
    }

    /** Orders slots by the first-seen position of their earliest member, matching the order
     * children were first encountered across all samples (same convention as the old flat loop). */
    static List<Slot> group(ElementNode parent) {
        List<ElementNode> children = parent.childrenInInferredOrder();
        Map<QName, Integer> order = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < children.size(); i++) {
            order.put(children.get(i).qname, i);
        }

        List<ElementNode> candidates = new ArrayList<>();
        for (ElementNode child : children) {
            if (child.presentInParentInstances > 0 && child.presentInParentInstances < parent.totalInstances) {
                candidates.add(child);
            }
        }

        int[] parentOf = new int[candidates.size()];
        for (int i = 0; i < parentOf.length; i++) {
            parentOf[i] = i;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < candidates.size(); i++) {
            for (int j = i + 1; j < candidates.size(); j++) {
                if (neverCoOccur(parent, candidates.get(i).qname, candidates.get(j).qname)) {
                    union(parentOf, i, j);
                }
            }
        }

        Map<Integer, List<ElementNode>> groupsByRoot = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < candidates.size(); i++) {
            groupsByRoot.computeIfAbsent(find(parentOf, i), k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(candidates.get(i));
        }

        Set<ElementNode> grouped = new java.util.HashSet<>();
        List<Slot> slots = new ArrayList<>();
        for (List<ElementNode> members : groupsByRoot.values()) {
            if (members.size() < 2) {
                continue;
            }
            grouped.addAll(members);
            slots.add(new ChoiceSlot(members, isRequired(parent, members)));
        }
        for (ElementNode child : children) {
            if (!grouped.contains(child)) {
                slots.add(new SingleSlot(child));
            }
        }

        slots.sort((a, b) -> Integer.compare(firstPosition(a, order), firstPosition(b, order)));
        return slots;
    }

    private static int firstPosition(Slot slot, Map<QName, Integer> order) {
        List<ElementNode> members = slot instanceof SingleSlot s ? List.of(s.child()) : ((ChoiceSlot) slot).members();
        int min = Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        for (ElementNode m : members) {
            min = Math.min(min, order.getOrDefault(m.qname, Integer.MAX_VALUE));
        }
        return min;
    }

    private static boolean neverCoOccur(ElementNode parent, QName a, QName b) {
        if (parent.occurrenceChildSets.isEmpty()) {
            return false;
        }
        for (Set<QName> present : parent.occurrenceChildSets) {
            if (present.contains(a) && present.contains(b)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    /** A choice group is "required" only if we have full (uncapped) occurrence data for the
     * parent and at least one member is present in every single recorded occurrence. */
    private static boolean isRequired(ElementNode parent, List<ElementNode> members) {
        if (!parent.hasCompleteOccurrenceData() || parent.occurrenceChildSets.isEmpty()) {
            return false;
        }
        Set<QName> names = new java.util.HashSet<>();
        for (ElementNode m : members) {
            names.add(m.qname);
        }
        for (Set<QName> present : parent.occurrenceChildSets) {
            boolean anyPresent = false;
            for (QName n : names) {
                if (present.contains(n)) {
                    anyPresent = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (!anyPresent) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    private static int find(int[] parentOf, int i) {
        while (parentOf[i] != i) {
            i = parentOf[i];
        }
        return i;
    }

    private static void union(int[] parentOf, int i, int j) {
        int ri = find(parentOf, i);
        int rj = find(parentOf, j);
        if (ri != rj) {
            parentOf[ri] = rj;
        }
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/DatatypeGuesser.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/** Guesses an XSD datatype from observed leaf text values; falls back to xs:string. */
final class DatatypeGuesser {

    private static final Pattern INTEGER = Pattern.compile("-?\\d+");
    private static final Pattern DECIMAL = Pattern.compile("-?\\d+\\.\\d+");

    private DatatypeGuesser() {
    }

    static String guess(List<String> samples) {
        return guess(samples, "");
    }

    /** {@code localName} applies the ISO 20022 tag-name conventions (see {@link TagNameRules})
     * as a hint before falling back to pure value-sniffing -- most importantly, an Id/Ref/Nb
     * field is kept as xs:string even when every sample happens to look numeric, since coercing
     * it to a numeric type would be lossy for values with leading zeros. */
    static String guess(List<String> samples, String localName) {
        TagNameRules.Hint hint = TagNameRules.hintFor(localName);
        if (hint == TagNameRules.Hint.TEXT_KEEP_LEADING_ZEROS) {
            return "string";
        }
        if (samples.isEmpty()) {
            return "string";
        }
        if (hint == TagNameRules.Hint.BOOLEAN && allMatch(samples, s -> s.equals("true") || s.equals("false"))) {
            return "boolean";
        }
        if (hint == TagNameRules.Hint.DATE && allMatch(samples, DatatypeGuesser::isDate)) {
            return "date";
        }
        if (hint == TagNameRules.Hint.DATE_TIME && allMatch(samples, DatatypeGuesser::isDateTime)) {
            return "dateTime";
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, s -> s.equals("true") || s.equals("false"))) {
            return "boolean";
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, s -> INTEGER.matcher(s).matches() && fitsInt(s))) {
            return "integer";
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, s -> INTEGER.matcher(s).matches())) {
            return "long";
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, s -> DECIMAL.matcher(s).matches())) {
            return "decimal";
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, DatatypeGuesser::isDate)) {
            return "date";
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, DatatypeGuesser::isDateTime)) {
            return "dateTime";
        }
        return "string";
    }

    private static boolean fitsInt(String s) {
        try {
            Long.parseLong(s);
            long v = Long.parseLong(s);
            return v >= Integer.MIN_VALUE && v <= Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    private static boolean isDate(String s) {
        try {
            DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE.parse(s);
            return true;
        } catch (DateTimeParseException e) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    private static boolean isDateTime(String s) {
        try {
            DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME.parse(s);
            return true;
        } catch (DateTimeParseException e) {
            try {
                DateTimeFormatter.ISO_OFFSET_DATE_TIME.parse(s);
                return true;
            } catch (DateTimeParseException e2) {
                return false;
            }
        }
    }

    private static boolean allMatch(List<String> samples, java.util.function.Predicate<String> predicate) {
        for (String s : samples) {
            if (s.isEmpty() || !predicate.test(s)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/ElementNode.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import javax.xml.namespace.QName;
import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Deque;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Aggregated, cross-file statistics for one element position in the inferred tree.
 * {@code totalInstances} / {@code presentInParentInstances} are counted per-occurrence
 * (not per-file), so repeated elements and optionality are both order-independent of how
 * the samples were scanned.
 */
final class ElementNode {

    static final int MAX_SAMPLES = 300;

    final QName qname;
    final Map<QName, ElementNode> children = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    final Map<String, AttrNode> attributes = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    final List<String> textSamples = new ArrayList<>();
    /** One entry per occurrence of this node, holding which direct children were present --
     * used to detect xs:choice (children that never co-occur but collectively cover every
     * occurrence). Capped like textSamples since only a bounded sample is needed to decide. */
    final List<Set<QName>> occurrenceChildSets = new ArrayList<>();
    /** key comes before value, observed in at least one occurrence -- used to recover the real
     * declared sequence order, since samples can discover an optional early child late (the
     * first-scanned sample may simply be missing it) and plain first-seen order would then put
     * it after children that must actually come before it. */
    final Map<QName, Set<QName>> before = new HashMap<>();

    int totalInstances;
    int presentInParentInstances;
    int maxRepeatPerInstance = 1;
    boolean hasChildren;
    int filesPresentIn;

    ElementNode(QName qname) {
        this.qname = qname;
    }

    void addTextSample(String text) {
        if (textSamples.size() < MAX_SAMPLES) {
            textSamples.add(text);
        }
    }

    void addOccurrenceChildSet(Set<QName> present) {
        if (occurrenceChildSets.size() < MAX_SAMPLES) {
            occurrenceChildSets.add(new LinkedHashSet<>(present));
        }
    }

    /** True only if every recorded occurrence of this node was captured (the cap wasn't hit),
     * so choice coverage computed from {@link #occurrenceChildSets} is exact, not a sample. */
    boolean hasCompleteOccurrenceData() {
        return occurrenceChildSets.size() == totalInstances;
    }

    void addOrderEdges(List<QName> orderedDistinctChildren) {
        for (int i = 0; i < orderedDistinctChildren.size(); i++) {
            QName a = orderedDistinctChildren.get(i);
            Set<QName> after = before.computeIfAbsent(a, k -> new LinkedHashSet<>());
            for (int j = i + 1; j < orderedDistinctChildren.size(); j++) {
                after.add(orderedDistinctChildren.get(j));
            }
        }
    }

    /** Topologically sorts {@link #children} using the "before" edges collected from every
     * sample, falling back to first-seen (map insertion) order wherever samples gave no
     * constraint or disagreed (a cycle), so the result degrades gracefully to the old behavior
     * rather than failing. */
    List<ElementNode> childrenInInferredOrder() {
        List<QName> firstSeen = new ArrayList<>(children.keySet());
        Map<QName, Integer> indegree = new HashMap<>();
        for (QName q : firstSeen) {
            indegree.put(q, 0);
        }
        for (QName a : firstSeen) {
            for (QName b : before.getOrDefault(a, Set.of())) {
                if (indegree.containsKey(b)) {
                    indegree.merge(b, 1, Integer::sum);
                }
            }
        }

        List<QName> ordered = new ArrayList<>();
        Set<QName> placed = new HashSet<>();
        Deque<QName> remaining = new ArrayDeque<>(firstSeen);
        while (!remaining.isEmpty()) {
            QName next = null;
            for (QName q : remaining) {
                if (indegree.get(q) == 0) {
                    next = q;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (next == null) {
                // Cycle (conflicting order evidence across samples): take the earliest
                // first-seen remaining node rather than getting stuck.
                next = remaining.peek();
            }
            ordered.add(next);
            placed.add(next);
            remaining.remove(next);
            for (QName b : before.getOrDefault(next, Set.of())) {
                if (indegree.containsKey(b) && !placed.contains(b)) {
                    indegree.merge(b, -1, Integer::sum);
                }
            }
        }

        List<ElementNode> result = new ArrayList<>(ordered.size());
        for (QName q : ordered) {
            result.add(children.get(q));
        }
        return result;
    }

    boolean isRequired(int parentTotalInstances) {
        return presentInParentInstances == parentTotalInstances && presentInParentInstances > 0;
    }

    boolean repeats() {
        return maxRepeatPerInstance > 1;
    }

    static final class AttrNode {
        final String name;
        final List<String> valueSamples = new ArrayList<>();
        int presentCount;

        AttrNode(String name) {
            this.name = name;
        }

        void addSample(String value) {
            if (valueSamples.size() < MAX_SAMPLES) {
                valueSamples.add(value);
            }
        }

        boolean isRequired(int ownerTotalInstances) {
            return presentCount == ownerTotalInstances && presentCount > 0;
        }
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/FormatDetector.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/**
 * Detects a handful of well-known ISO/SWIFT value formats directly from sample values, with
 * their own checksum where one exists. These are reported at "high" confidence (auto-accepted,
 * not shown in the review list) since the checksum (or the fixed ISO 4217/3166 code list)
 * confirms the guess far more strongly than a bare regex match would.
 */
final class FormatDetector {

    enum Format { ISIN, BIC, LEI, CURRENCY, COUNTRY, ISO_DATE, NONE }

    private static final Pattern ISIN = Pattern.compile("[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{9}[0-9]");
    private static final Pattern BIC = Pattern.compile("[A-Z]{6}[A-Z0-9]{2}([A-Z0-9]{3})?");
    private static final Pattern LEI = Pattern.compile("[0-9A-Z]{18}[0-9]{2}");

    private static final Set<String> ISO_4217 = Set.of(
            "USD", "EUR", "GBP", "JPY", "CHF", "INR", "AUD", "CAD", "SGD", "HKD", "CNY", "NZD", "SEK", "NOK", "ZAR");
    private static final Set<String> ISO_3166 = Set.of(
            "US", "GB", "DE", "FR", "JP", "IN", "AU", "CA", "SG", "HK", "NL", "CH", "CN", "NZ", "SE", "NO", "ZA");

    private FormatDetector() {
    }

    /** Only returns a format when EVERY sample matches it -- a single counter-example falls
     * through to the ordinary datatype guess rather than a wrong high-confidence claim. */
    static Format detect(List<String> samples) {
        if (samples.isEmpty()) {
            return Format.NONE;
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, FormatDetector::isIsin)) {
            return Format.ISIN;
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, s -> BIC.matcher(s).matches())) {
            return Format.BIC;
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, FormatDetector::isLei)) {
            return Format.LEI;
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, s -> ISO_4217.contains(s))) {
            return Format.CURRENCY;
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, s -> ISO_3166.contains(s))) {
            return Format.COUNTRY;
        }
        if (allMatch(samples, FormatDetector::isIsoDate)) {
            return Format.ISO_DATE;
        }
        return Format.NONE;
    }

    private static boolean isIsin(String s) {
        if (!ISIN.matcher(s).matches()) {
            return false;
        }
        return isinCheckDigit(s) == (s.charAt(11) - '0');
    }

    /** ISO 6166 check digit: Luhn mod 10 over the string with letters expanded to two digits
     * (A=10 .. Z=35) and the trailing check digit dropped before computing. */
    private static int isinCheckDigit(String isin) {
        StringBuilder digits = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < isin.length() - 1; i++) {
            char c = isin.charAt(i);
            if (Character.isDigit(c)) {
                digits.append(c);
            } else {
                digits.append(c - 'A' + 10);
            }
        }
        int sum = 0;
        boolean doubleIt = digits.length() % 2 != 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < digits.length(); i++) {
            int d = digits.charAt(i) - '0';
            if (doubleIt) {
                d *= 2;
                if (d > 9) {
                    d -= 9;
                }
            }
            sum += d;
            doubleIt = !doubleIt;
        }
        return (10 - (sum % 10)) % 10;
    }

    /** LEI check digits (ISO 17442) are a mod-97 check over the 18-character prefix, same
     * letter-to-number expansion as IBAN ("00" appended before taking mod 97). */
    private static boolean isLei(String s) {
        if (!LEI.matcher(s).matches()) {
            return false;
        }
        StringBuilder expanded = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < 18; i++) {
            char c = s.charAt(i);
            expanded.append(Character.isDigit(c) ? String.valueOf(c) : String.valueOf(c - 'A' + 10));
        }
        expanded.append("00");
        BigInteger remainder = new BigInteger(expanded.toString()).mod(BigInteger.valueOf(97));
        int checkDigits = Integer.parseInt(s.substring(18));
        return (98 - remainder.intValue()) == checkDigits;
    }

    private static boolean isIsoDate(String s) {
        try {
            DateTimeFormatter.ISO_LOCAL_DATE.parse(s);
            return true;
        } catch (DateTimeParseException e) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    private static boolean allMatch(List<String> samples, java.util.function.Predicate<String> predicate) {
        for (String s : samples) {
            if (s.isEmpty() || !predicate.test(s)) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }
}

package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import com.project.toolkit.validate.XsdValidatorCache;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

public final class InferCommand {

    public static void run(InferOptions opts) throws IOException {
        List<Path> xmlFiles = collectXmlFiles(opts.xmlInput);
        if (xmlFiles.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No .xml files found at " + opts.xmlInput);
        }

        XmlStructureScanner scanner = new XmlStructureScanner();
        ElementNode root = scanner.scan(xmlFiles);

        if (opts.outXsd.getParent() != null) {
            Files.createDirectories(opts.outXsd.getParent());
        }
        XsdWriter xsdWriter = new XsdWriter();
        xsdWriter.write(root, opts.outXsd);
        System.out.println("  complexTypes: " + xsdWriter.typeCountAfterMerge()
                + " (before merging structurally identical types: " + xsdWriter.typeCountBeforeMerge() + ")");

        String reportName = stripExtension(opts.outXsd.getFileName().toString()) + "_review.md";
        Path reportPath = opts.outXsd.resolveSibling(reportName);
        if (opts.baselineXsd != null) {
            new ReviewReportWriter().writeWithBaseline(root, scanner.fileCount, reportPath, opts.baselineXsd);
        } else {
            new ReviewReportWriter().write(root, scanner.fileCount, reportPath);
        }

        System.out.println("Review report: " + reportPath);
        System.out.println("Validating " + xmlFiles.size() + " input XML(s) against the inferred XSD...");
        int valid = 0;
        for (Path xml : xmlFiles) {
            var result = XsdValidatorCache.validate(opts.outXsd, xml);
            if (result.valid()) {
                valid++;
            } else {
                System.out.println("  [FAIL] " + xml.getFileName() + ": " + result.reason());
            }
        }
        System.out.println("  " + valid + " / " + xmlFiles.size() + " valid against the inferred XSD");
    }

    private static List<Path> collectXmlFiles(Path input) throws IOException {
        List<Path> files = new ArrayList<>();
        if (Files.isDirectory(input)) {
            try (Stream<Path> stream = Files.list(input)) {
                stream.filter(p -> p.toString().endsWith(".xml"))
                        .sorted(Comparator.naturalOrder())
                        .forEach(files::add);
            }
        } else {
            files.add(input);
        }
        return files;
    }

    private static String stripExtension(String fileName) {
        int dot = fileName.lastIndexOf('.');
        return dot > 0 ? fileName.substring(0, dot) : fileName;
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/InferOptions.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import java.nio.file.Path;

public final class InferOptions {
    public Path xmlInput;
    public Path outXsd;
    public Path baselineXsd;

    public static InferOptions parse(String[] args) {
        InferOptions opts = new InferOptions();
        for (int i = 0; i < args.length; i++) {
            switch (args[i]) {
                case "--xml" -> opts.xmlInput = Path.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--xml"));
                case "--out" -> opts.outXsd = Path.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--out"));
                case "--baseline" -> opts.baselineXsd = Path.of(requireValue(args, ++i, "--baseline"));
                default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown option: " + args[i]);
            }
        }
        if (opts.xmlInput == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--xml is required");
        }
        if (opts.outXsd == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--out is required");
        }
        if (!java.nio.file.Files.exists(opts.xmlInput)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("--xml path not found: " + opts.xmlInput);
        }
        return opts;
    }

    private static String requireValue(String[] args, int index, String flag) {
        if (index >= args.length) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(flag + " requires a value");
        }
        return args[index];
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/ReviewItem.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

/** One reviewable guess the inferrer made, with enough evidence for a human to judge it. */
record ReviewItem(String path, Kind kind, String guess, String evidence, Confidence confidence) {

    enum Kind { REQUIRED_OPTIONAL, REPEATS, ENUMERATION, CHOICE, DATATYPE, FORMAT }

    enum Confidence { HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW }

    String toMarkdownLine() {
        return "- " + path + ": " + evidence + " -> " + guess + ". Please confirm.";
    }

    String toJson() {
        return "{\"path\":" + jsonString(path)
                + ",\"kind\":" + jsonString(kind.name())
                + ",\"guess\":" + jsonString(guess)
                + ",\"evidence\":" + jsonString(evidence)
                + ",\"confidence\":" + jsonString(confidence.name())
                + "}";
    }

    private static String jsonString(String s) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("\"");
        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
            char c = s.charAt(i);
            switch (c) {
                case '"' -> sb.append("\\\"");
                case '\\' -> sb.append("\\\\");
                case '\n' -> sb.append("\\n");
                default -> sb.append(c);
            }
        }
        return sb.append('"').toString();
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/ReviewReportWriter.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/** Writes a plain-language review report so a human can sanity-check the inferred XSD. */
final class ReviewReportWriter {

    private static final int ENUM_MIN_SAMPLES = 20;
    private static final int ENUM_MAX_DISTINCT = 6;
    private static final int ENUM_MIN_DISTINCT = 2;
    private static final int ENUM_MAX_VALUE_LENGTH = 12;
    private static final int MIN_CONFIDENT_SAMPLES = 5;

    private final List<ReviewItem> reviewItems = new ArrayList<>();
    private final List<ReviewItem> autoAccepted = new ArrayList<>();

    void write(ElementNode root, int fileCount, Path outReportMd) throws IOException {
        walk(root, fileCount, "", -1);
        writeMarkdown(fileCount, outReportMd, null);
        writeJson(fileCount, jsonPathFor(outReportMd), null);
    }

    /** Baseline mode: only reports what changed versus a previously-written XSD. */
    void writeWithBaseline(ElementNode root, int fileCount, Path outReportMd, Path baselineXsd) throws IOException {
        walk(root, fileCount, "", -1);
        List<BaselineDiff.Change> changes = BaselineDiff.diff(root, baselineXsd);
        writeMarkdown(fileCount, outReportMd, changes);
        writeJson(fileCount, jsonPathFor(outReportMd), changes);
    }

    private static Path jsonPathFor(Path outReportMd) {
        String name = outReportMd.getFileName().toString();
        String base = name.endsWith(".md") ? name.substring(0, name.length() - 3) : name;
        return outReportMd.resolveSibling(base + ".json");
    }

    private void writeMarkdown(int fileCount, Path outReport, List<BaselineDiff.Change> changes) throws IOException {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        sb.append("# XSD inference review\n\n");
        if (fileCount <= 1) {
            sb.append("> **Warning:** only ").append(fileCount).append(" sample file was given. ")
                    .append("Required-vs-optional and repeat guesses below are based on a single example ")
                    .append("and may not hold for other real files -- please review carefully.\n\n");
        } else {
            sb.append("Based on ").append(fileCount).append(" sample files. ")
                    .append(autoAccepted.size()).append(" high-confidence guess(es) were auto-accepted and are not listed below.\n\n");
        }

        if (changes != null) {
            sb.append("## Changes vs. baseline\n\n");
            if (changes.isEmpty()) {
                sb.append("(no differences from the baseline XSD)\n\n");
            } else {
                for (BaselineDiff.Change c : changes) {
                    sb.append("- ").append(c.path()).append(": ").append(c.kind())
                            .append(" (").append(c.before()).append(" -> ").append(c.after()).append(")\n");
                }
                sb.append('\n');
            }
            Files.writeString(outReport, sb.toString());
            return;
        }

        appendSection(sb, "Required/optional needing confirmation", ReviewItem.Kind.REQUIRED_OPTIONAL);
        appendSection(sb, "Repeats needing confirmation", ReviewItem.Kind.REPEATS);
        appendSection(sb, "Possible choice groups (mutually exclusive fields)", ReviewItem.Kind.CHOICE);
        appendSection(sb, "Possible enumerations", ReviewItem.Kind.ENUMERATION);

        Files.writeString(outReport, sb.toString());
    }

    private void appendSection(StringBuilder sb, String title, ReviewItem.Kind kind) {
        List<ReviewItem> items = reviewItems.stream().filter(i -> i.kind() == kind).toList();
        sb.append("## ").append(title).append("\n\n");
        if (items.isEmpty()) {
            sb.append("(none)\n\n");
        } else {
            for (ReviewItem item : items) {
                sb.append(item.toMarkdownLine()).append(" [confidence: ").append(item.confidence().name().toLowerCase()).append("]\n");
            }
            sb.append('\n');
        }
    }

    private void writeJson(int fileCount, Path outReportJson, List<BaselineDiff.Change> changes) throws IOException {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        sb.append("{\n  \"fileCount\":").append(fileCount).append(",\n");
        if (changes != null) {
            sb.append("  \"baselineChanges\":[");
            for (int i = 0; i < changes.size(); i++) {
                BaselineDiff.Change c = changes.get(i);
                sb.append(i == 0 ? "" : ",").append("\n    {\"path\":\"").append(escape(c.path()))
                        .append("\",\"kind\":\"").append(escape(c.kind()))
                        .append("\",\"before\":\"").append(escape(c.before()))
                        .append("\",\"after\":\"").append(escape(c.after())).append("\"}");
            }
            sb.append(changes.isEmpty() ? "]\n" : "\n  ]\n");
            sb.append("}\n");
            Files.writeString(outReportJson, sb.toString());
            return;
        }

        sb.append("  \"needsReview\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < reviewItems.size(); i++) {
            sb.append(i == 0 ? "" : ",").append("\n    ").append(reviewItems.get(i).toJson());
        }
        sb.append(reviewItems.isEmpty() ? "]" : "\n  ]").append(",\n");
        sb.append("  \"autoAccepted\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < autoAccepted.size(); i++) {
            sb.append(i == 0 ? "" : ",").append("\n    ").append(autoAccepted.get(i).toJson());
        }
        sb.append(autoAccepted.isEmpty() ? "]\n" : "\n  ]\n");
        sb.append("}\n");
        Files.writeString(outReportJson, sb.toString());
    }

    private static String escape(String s) {
        return s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\"", "\\\"");
    }

    private void walk(ElementNode node, int fileCount, String path, int parentTotalInstances) {
        String name = path.isEmpty() ? node.qname.getLocalPart() : path + "/" + node.qname.getLocalPart();
        boolean isRoot = parentTotalInstances < 0;

        if (!isRoot) {
            noteRequiredOptional(name, node, parentTotalInstances);
        }
        if (node.repeats()) {
            noteRepeats(name, node, fileCount);
        }
        noteEnumCandidate(name, node.qname.getLocalPart(), node.textSamples);

        for (ElementNode.AttrNode attr : node.attributes.values()) {
            String attrPath = name + "/@" + attr.name;
            noteAttrRequiredOptional(attrPath, attr, node.totalInstances);
            noteEnumCandidate(attrPath, attr.name, attr.valueSamples);
        }

        for (ChoiceGrouper.Slot slot : ChoiceGrouper.group(node)) {
            if (slot instanceof ChoiceGrouper.ChoiceSlot choice) {
                noteChoice(name, choice);
            }
        }

        for (ElementNode child : node.children.values()) {
            walk(child, fileCount, name, node.totalInstances);
        }
    }

    /** Required/optional is judged purely against the immediate parent's own occurrence count --
     * a child present every time its parent occurs is required, no question, and isn't listed.
     * An optional call is itself only "in doubt" (shown) when the sample size is small or the
     * split is a near-unanimous 1-occurrence outlier; a clean, well-sampled partial presence is
     * exactly what minOccurs="0" means and needs no confirmation. */
    private void noteRequiredOptional(String path, ElementNode node, int parentTotalInstances) {
        boolean required = node.isRequired(parentTotalInstances);
        if (required) {
            return;
        }
        int present = node.presentInParentInstances;
        int absent = parentTotalInstances - present;
        ReviewItem.Confidence confidence;
        if (parentTotalInstances < MIN_CONFIDENT_SAMPLES) {
            confidence = ReviewItem.Confidence.LOW;
        } else if (present <= 1 || absent <= 1) {
            confidence = ReviewItem.Confidence.MEDIUM;
        } else {
            confidence = ReviewItem.Confidence.HIGH;
        }
        String evidence = "present in " + present + " of " + parentTotalInstances + " occurrences of its parent";
        ReviewItem item = new ReviewItem(path, ReviewItem.Kind.REQUIRED_OPTIONAL, "optional", evidence, confidence);
        file(item);
    }

    private void noteAttrRequiredOptional(String path, ElementNode.AttrNode attr, int ownerTotalInstances) {
        boolean required = attr.isRequired(ownerTotalInstances);
        if (required) {
            return;
        }
        int absent = ownerTotalInstances - attr.presentCount;
        ReviewItem.Confidence confidence;
        if (ownerTotalInstances < MIN_CONFIDENT_SAMPLES) {
            confidence = ReviewItem.Confidence.LOW;
        } else if (attr.presentCount <= 1 || absent <= 1) {
            confidence = ReviewItem.Confidence.MEDIUM;
        } else {
            confidence = ReviewItem.Confidence.HIGH;
        }
        String evidence = "present on " + attr.presentCount + " of " + ownerTotalInstances + " occurrences";
        file(new ReviewItem(path, ReviewItem.Kind.REQUIRED_OPTIONAL, "optional attribute", evidence, confidence));
    }

    private void noteRepeats(String path, ElementNode node, int fileCount) {
        ReviewItem.Confidence confidence = node.totalInstances < MIN_CONFIDENT_SAMPLES
                ? ReviewItem.Confidence.LOW : ReviewItem.Confidence.HIGH;
        String evidence = "repeats up to " + node.maxRepeatPerInstance + " times in a single occurrence";
        file(new ReviewItem(path, ReviewItem.Kind.REPEATS, "maxOccurs=unbounded", evidence, confidence));
    }

    private void noteChoice(String parentPath, ChoiceGrouper.ChoiceSlot choice) {
        StringBuilder names = new StringBuilder();
        for (ElementNode member : choice.members()) {
            if (names.length() > 0) {
                names.append(", ");
            }
            names.append(member.qname.getLocalPart());
        }
        ReviewItem.Confidence confidence = choice.required() ? ReviewItem.Confidence.MEDIUM : ReviewItem.Confidence.LOW;
        file(new ReviewItem(parentPath, ReviewItem.Kind.CHOICE, "xs:choice(" + names + ")",
                "these fields never appear together in the same occurrence", confidence));
    }

    private void noteEnumCandidate(String path, String localName, List<String> samples) {
        if (TagNameRules.isIdentifierLike(localName)) {
            return;
        }
        if (FormatDetector.detect(samples) != FormatDetector.Format.NONE) {
            // A recognized format (ISIN/BIC/LEI/currency/country/date) is a stronger, more useful
            // claim than "looks like an enum" and is auto-accepted elsewhere; don't also suggest
            // treating it as a closed value list.
            return;
        }
        String guessedType = DatatypeGuesser.guess(samples, localName);
        if (guessedType.equals("decimal") || guessedType.equals("integer") || guessedType.equals("long")
                || guessedType.equals("date") || guessedType.equals("dateTime") || guessedType.equals("boolean")) {
            return;
        }
        if (samples.size() < ENUM_MIN_SAMPLES) {
            return;
        }
        Set<String> distinct = new LinkedHashSet<>(samples);
        if (distinct.size() < ENUM_MIN_DISTINCT || distinct.size() > ENUM_MAX_DISTINCT) {
            return;
        }
        for (String v : distinct) {
            if (v.length() > ENUM_MAX_VALUE_LENGTH) {
                return;
            }
        }
        Map<String, Integer> counts = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        for (String s : samples) {
            counts.merge(s, 1, Integer::sum);
        }
        for (int c : counts.values()) {
            if (c < 2) {
                return;
            }
        }
        String evidence = samples.size() + " samples, " + distinct.size() + " distinct values seen, each at least twice";
        file(new ReviewItem(path, ReviewItem.Kind.ENUMERATION, "enum(" + String.join(", ", distinct) + ")", evidence, ReviewItem.Confidence.MEDIUM));
    }

    private void file(ReviewItem item) {
        if (item.confidence() == ReviewItem.Confidence.HIGH) {
            autoAccepted.add(item);
        } else {
            reviewItems.add(item);
        }
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/TagNameRules.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

/**
 * ISO 20022-style naming conventions used as a hint for the leaf datatype, applied before
 * falling back to pure value-sniffing in {@link DatatypeGuesser}. These are suffix/prefix
 * conventions used across the SWIFT/ISO 20022 message family (not specific to any one schema).
 */
final class TagNameRules {

    enum Hint {
        DATE, DATE_TIME, AMOUNT, BOOLEAN, TEXT_KEEP_LEADING_ZEROS, CODE, NONE
    }

    private TagNameRules() {
    }

    static Hint hintFor(String localName) {
        String n = localName;
        if (n.endsWith("DtTm")) {
            return Hint.DATE_TIME;
        }
        if (n.endsWith("Dt")) {
            return Hint.DATE;
        }
        if (n.endsWith("Ind") || n.endsWith("Flg")) {
            return Hint.BOOLEAN;
        }
        if (n.endsWith("Amt")) {
            return Hint.AMOUNT;
        }
        if (n.endsWith("Id") || n.endsWith("Ref") || n.endsWith("Nb")) {
            return Hint.TEXT_KEEP_LEADING_ZEROS;
        }
        if (n.endsWith("Cd") || n.endsWith("Tp")) {
            return Hint.CODE;
        }
        return Hint.NONE;
    }

    /** True for the Id/Ref/Nb family -- used to keep these out of enumeration suggestions too,
     * since a reference number repeating a handful of times across a small sample is coincidence,
     * not a closed value set. */
    static boolean isIdentifierLike(String localName) {
        return hintFor(localName) == Hint.TEXT_KEEP_LEADING_ZEROS;
    }

    static boolean isAmountField(String localName) {
        return hintFor(localName) == Hint.AMOUNT;
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/XmlStructureScanner.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import javax.xml.namespace.QName;
import javax.xml.stream.XMLInputFactory;
import javax.xml.stream.XMLStreamConstants;
import javax.xml.stream.XMLStreamReader;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Deque;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Reads one or more sample XMLs with StAX and merges them into a single tree of
 * {@link ElementNode}s, tracking per-occurrence presence so required/optional and
 * maxOccurs can be inferred across all samples at once.
 */
final class XmlStructureScanner {

    private ElementNode root;
    int fileCount;

    ElementNode scan(List<Path> xmlFiles) throws IOException {
        XMLInputFactory inputFactory = XMLInputFactory.newInstance();
        inputFactory.setProperty(XMLInputFactory.IS_COALESCING, true);
        for (Path file : xmlFiles) {
            scanOne(file, inputFactory);
            fileCount++;
        }
        return root;
    }

    private void scanOne(Path file, XMLInputFactory inputFactory) throws IOException {
        Deque<Frame> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();
        Set<ElementNode> seenThisFile = new HashSet<>();
        try (InputStream in = Files.newInputStream(file)) {
            XMLStreamReader reader = inputFactory.createXMLStreamReader(in);
            while (reader.hasNext()) {
                int event = reader.next();
                if (event == XMLStreamConstants.START_ELEMENT) {
                    handleStart(reader, stack, seenThisFile);
                } else if (event == XMLStreamConstants.CHARACTERS || event == XMLStreamConstants.CDATA) {
                    if (!stack.isEmpty()) {
                        stack.peek().text.append(reader.getText());
                    }
                } else if (event == XMLStreamConstants.END_ELEMENT) {
                    handleEnd(stack);
                }
            }
            reader.close();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new IOException("Failed reading " + file + ": " + e.getMessage(), e);
        }
        for (ElementNode node : seenThisFile) {
            node.filesPresentIn++;
        }
    }

    private void handleStart(XMLStreamReader reader, Deque<Frame> stack, Set<ElementNode> seenThisFile) {
        QName qname = reader.getName();
        ElementNode node;
        if (stack.isEmpty()) {
            if (root == null) {
                root = new ElementNode(qname);
            }
            node = root;
        } else {
            Frame parentFrame = stack.peek();
            parentFrame.childCounts.merge(qname, 1, Integer::sum);
            parentFrame.childOrder.add(qname);
            node = parentFrame.node.children.computeIfAbsent(qname, ElementNode::new);
        }
        node.totalInstances++;
        seenThisFile.add(node);

        for (int i = 0; i < reader.getAttributeCount(); i++) {
            String attrName = reader.getAttributeLocalName(i);
            ElementNode.AttrNode attr = node.attributes.computeIfAbsent(attrName, ElementNode.AttrNode::new);
            attr.presentCount++;
            attr.addSample(reader.getAttributeValue(i));
        }

        stack.push(new Frame(node));
    }

    private void handleEnd(Deque<Frame> stack) {
        Frame finished = stack.pop();
        ElementNode node = finished.node;
        if (!finished.childCounts.isEmpty()) {
            node.hasChildren = true;
            node.addOccurrenceChildSet(finished.childCounts.keySet());
            node.addOrderEdges(new ArrayList<>(finished.childOrder));
            for (Map.Entry<QName, Integer> entry : finished.childCounts.entrySet()) {
                ElementNode child = node.children.get(entry.getKey());
                child.presentInParentInstances++;
                child.maxRepeatPerInstance = Math.max(child.maxRepeatPerInstance, entry.getValue());
            }
        } else {
            String text = finished.text.toString().trim();
            if (!text.isEmpty()) {
                node.addTextSample(text);
            }
        }
    }

    private static final class Frame {
        final ElementNode node;
        final Map<QName, Integer> childCounts = new HashMap<>();
        final Set<QName> childOrder = new LinkedHashSet<>();
        final StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder();

        Frame(ElementNode node) {
            this.node = node;
        }
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/infer/XsdWriter.java ===
package com.project.toolkit.infer;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.IdentityHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * Renders the merged {@link ElementNode} tree as a plain hand-readable XSD: one named
 * complexType per element that has children or attributes, xs:sequence preserving the
 * order elements were first seen in, and inline xs:string/xs:decimal/... for leaves.
 */
final class XsdWriter {

    private final Map<ElementNode, String> typeNames = new IdentityHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Integer> nameCounts = new HashMap<>();
    private final List<String> complexTypeBlocks = new ArrayList<>();
    private final Map<String, String> typeByStructuralKey = new HashMap<>();
    private String typePrefix = "";
    private String schemaNamespace = "";
    private int typeCountBeforeMerge;

    /** Number of element positions that needed a named complexType, before deduplicating
     * structurally identical ones -- set after {@link #write}. */
    int typeCountBeforeMerge() {
        return typeCountBeforeMerge;
    }

    /** Final number of distinct named complexTypes actually written -- set after {@link #write}. */
    int typeCountAfterMerge() {
        return complexTypeBlocks.size();
    }

    void write(ElementNode root, Path outXsd) throws IOException {
        String ns = root.qname.getNamespaceURI();
        schemaNamespace = ns == null ? "" : ns;
        if (ns != null && !ns.isEmpty()) {
            // Named complexTypes live in the target namespace, so references to them need the
            // "tns:" prefix -- an unprefixed type="DocumentType" would resolve to no namespace.
            typePrefix = "tns:";
        }
        assignTypes(root);

        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        sb.append("<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n");
        sb.append("<xs:schema xmlns:xs=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema\"");
        if (ns != null && !ns.isEmpty()) {
            sb.append(" xmlns:tns=\"").append(ns).append("\"")
                    .append(" targetNamespace=\"").append(ns).append("\"")
                    .append(" elementFormDefault=\"qualified\"");
        }
        sb.append(">\n\n");

        String rootTypeRef = typeNames.containsKey(root)
                ? typePrefix + typeNames.get(root)
                : "xs:" + DatatypeGuesser.guess(root.textSamples, root.qname.getLocalPart());
        sb.append("  <xs:element name=\"").append(root.qname.getLocalPart())
                .append("\" type=\"").append(rootTypeRef).append("\"/>\n\n");

        for (String block : complexTypeBlocks) {
            sb.append(block).append('\n');
        }
        sb.append("</xs:schema>\n");

        Files.writeString(outXsd, sb.toString());
    }

    private void assignTypes(ElementNode node) {
        if (typeNames.containsKey(node)) {
            return;
        }
        for (ElementNode child : node.children.values()) {
            assignTypes(child);
        }
        if (node.hasChildren || !node.attributes.isEmpty()) {
            typeCountBeforeMerge++;
            // Computed after children are resolved above, so it already reflects any merging
            // done lower in the tree -- two parents whose children turned out to share a merged
            // type can now also be recognized as structurally identical to each other.
            String key = structuralKey(node);
            String existing = typeByStructuralKey.get(key);
            if (existing != null) {
                typeNames.put(node, existing);
                return;
            }
            String typeName = newTypeName(node.qname.getLocalPart());
            typeNames.put(node, typeName);
            typeByStructuralKey.put(key, typeName);
            complexTypeBlocks.add(renderComplexType(typeName, node));
        }
    }

    /** Same shape used for rendering (hasChildren/simpleContent, slot grouping, attributes), so
     * two nodes get the same key exactly when {@link #renderComplexType} would emit the same
     * complexType body for them -- that's the definition of "structurally identical" used here. */
    private String structuralKey(ElementNode node) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        if (node.hasChildren) {
            sb.append("SEQ[");
            for (ChoiceGrouper.Slot slot : ChoiceGrouper.group(node)) {
                if (slot instanceof ChoiceGrouper.SingleSlot single) {
                    sb.append(elementKey(single.child(), node, true));
                } else {
                    ChoiceGrouper.ChoiceSlot choice = (ChoiceGrouper.ChoiceSlot) slot;
                    sb.append("CHOICE(").append(choice.required()).append(")[");
                    for (ElementNode member : choice.members()) {
                        sb.append(elementKey(member, node, false));
                    }
                    sb.append(']');
                }
            }
            sb.append(']');
        } else {
            sb.append("SIMPLE(").append(DatatypeGuesser.guess(node.textSamples, node.qname.getLocalPart())).append(')');
        }
        sb.append("ATTRS[");
        for (ElementNode.AttrNode attr : node.attributes.values()) {
            sb.append(attr.name).append(':').append(DatatypeGuesser.guess(attr.valueSamples, attr.name))
                    .append(':').append(attr.isRequired(node.totalInstances)).append(';');
        }
        sb.append(']');
        return sb.toString();
    }

    private String elementKey(ElementNode child, ElementNode parent, boolean withMinOccurs) {
        String typeKey = typeNames.containsKey(child)
                ? typeNames.get(child)
                : "xs:" + DatatypeGuesser.guess(child.textSamples, child.qname.getLocalPart());
        boolean required = withMinOccurs && child.isRequired(parent.totalInstances);
        return child.qname.getLocalPart() + ":" + typeKey + ":" + required + ":" + child.repeats() + ";";
    }

    private String newTypeName(String local) {
        String base = capitalize(local) + "Type";
        int n = nameCounts.merge(base, 1, Integer::sum);
        return n == 1 ? base : base + "_" + n;
    }

    private String renderComplexType(String typeName, ElementNode node) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        sb.append("  <xs:complexType name=\"").append(typeName).append("\">\n");

        if (node.hasChildren) {
            sb.append("    <xs:sequence>\n");
            for (ChoiceGrouper.Slot slot : ChoiceGrouper.group(node)) {
                if (slot instanceof ChoiceGrouper.SingleSlot single) {
                    appendElementRef(sb, single.child(), node, "      ", true);
                } else {
                    ChoiceGrouper.ChoiceSlot choice = (ChoiceGrouper.ChoiceSlot) slot;
                    sb.append("      <xs:choice");
                    if (!choice.required()) {
                        sb.append(" minOccurs=\"0\"");
                    }
                    sb.append(" maxOccurs=\"unbounded\">\n");
                    for (ElementNode member : choice.members()) {
                        appendElementRef(sb, member, node, "        ", false);
                    }
                    sb.append("      </xs:choice>\n");
                }
            }
            sb.append("    </xs:sequence>\n");
            appendAttributes(sb, node);
        } else {
            String base = "xs:" + DatatypeGuesser.guess(node.textSamples, node.qname.getLocalPart());
            sb.append("    <xs:simpleContent>\n");
            sb.append("      <xs:extension base=\"").append(base).append("\">\n");
            for (ElementNode.AttrNode attr : node.attributes.values()) {
                appendAttribute(sb, attr, node.totalInstances, "        ");
            }
            sb.append("      </xs:extension>\n");
            sb.append("    </xs:simpleContent>\n");
        }

        sb.append("  </xs:complexType>\n");
        return sb.toString();
    }

    /** Renders one xs:element reference. {@code withMinOccurs} is false for a choice member,
     * since the enclosing xs:choice already carries the optionality for the whole group. */
    private void appendElementRef(StringBuilder sb, ElementNode child, ElementNode parent, String indent, boolean withMinOccurs) {
        String typeRef = typeNames.containsKey(child)
                ? typePrefix + typeNames.get(child)
                : "xs:" + DatatypeGuesser.guess(child.textSamples, child.qname.getLocalPart());
        sb.append(indent).append("<xs:element name=\"").append(child.qname.getLocalPart())
                .append("\" type=\"").append(typeRef).append("\"");
        String childNs = child.qname.getNamespaceURI();
        if (!schemaNamespace.isEmpty() && (childNs == null || childNs.isEmpty())) {
            // Observed unqualified in the samples (e.g. a filler written inside an xs:any slot)
            // even though the schema otherwise declares elementFormDefault="qualified".
            sb.append(" form=\"unqualified\"");
        }
        if (withMinOccurs && !child.isRequired(parent.totalInstances)) {
            sb.append(" minOccurs=\"0\"");
        }
        if (child.repeats()) {
            sb.append(" maxOccurs=\"unbounded\"");
        }
        sb.append("/>\n");
    }

    private void appendAttributes(StringBuilder sb, ElementNode node) {
        for (ElementNode.AttrNode attr : node.attributes.values()) {
            appendAttribute(sb, attr, node.totalInstances, "    ");
        }
    }

    private void appendAttribute(StringBuilder sb, ElementNode.AttrNode attr, int ownerTotalInstances, String indent) {
        String type = "xs:" + DatatypeGuesser.guess(attr.valueSamples, attr.name);
        boolean required = attr.isRequired(ownerTotalInstances);
        sb.append(indent).append("<xs:attribute name=\"").append(attr.name)
                .append("\" type=\"").append(type).append("\"")
                .append(" use=\"").append(required ? "required" : "optional").append("\"/>\n");
    }

    private static String capitalize(String s) {
        if (s.isEmpty()) {
            return s;
        }
        return Character.toUpperCase(s.charAt(0)) + s.substring(1);
    }
}

@@@=== FILE START: xml-toolkit/src/main/java/com/project/toolkit/ToolkitMain.java ===
package com.project.toolkit;

import com.project.toolkit.generate.GenerateCommand;
import com.project.toolkit.generate.GenerateOptions;
import com.project.toolkit.generate.GenerateResult;
import com.project.toolkit.generate.ScanCommand;
import com.project.toolkit.generate.SchemaScanResult;
import com.project.toolkit.infer.InferCommand;
import com.project.toolkit.infer.InferOptions;
import java.nio.file.Path;

public final class ToolkitMain {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        if (args.length == 0) {
            printUsage();
            System.exit(1);
        }
        String command = args[0];
        String[] rest = java.util.Arrays.copyOfRange(args, 1, args.length);
        try {
            switch (command) {
                case "generate" -> runGenerate(rest);
                case "infer" -> runInfer(rest);
                case "scan" -> runScan(rest);
                default -> {
                    System.err.println("Unknown command: " + command);
                    printUsage();
                    System.exit(1);
                }
            }
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
            System.err.println("Error: " + e.getMessage());
            System.exit(1);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.err.println("Error: " + e.getMessage());
            e.printStackTrace();
            System.exit(1);
        }
    }

    private static void runGenerate(String[] args) throws Exception {
        GenerateOptions opts = GenerateOptions.parse(args);
        // In "stream" mode, stdout IS the binary zip output -- human-readable status must not
        // share it, or it corrupts the stream for whatever is reading it downstream.
        java.io.PrintStream status = "stream".equals(opts.output) ? System.err : System.out;
        status.println("Generating " + opts.count + " XMLs from " + opts.xsd
                + (opts.out != null ? " into " + opts.out : "") + " ...");
        GenerateResult result = GenerateCommand.run(opts);
        status.println("Done.");
        result.print(status);
    }

    private static void runInfer(String[] args) throws Exception {
        InferOptions opts = InferOptions.parse(args);
        System.out.println("Inferring XSD from " + opts.xmlInput + " ...");
        InferCommand.run(opts);
        System.out.println("Done. Wrote " + opts.outXsd);
    }

    private static void runScan(String[] args) {
        if (args.length < 2 || !"--xsd".equals(args[0])) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("usage: scan --xsd <file>");
        }
        SchemaScanResult result = ScanCommand.run(Path.of(args[1]));
        result.print(System.out);
    }

    private static void printUsage() {
        System.out.println("""
                Usage:
                  java -jar xml-toolkit.jar generate --xsd <file> --out <folder> [--count N] [--size small|medium|large|mixed] [--seed N] [--level 1|2|3] [--profile <yaml>] [--output folder|zip|stream] [--threads N] [--error-percent N] [--error-types t1,t2] [--supplement <xsd>]
                  java -jar xml-toolkit.jar infer --xml <file or folder> --out <xsd file> [--baseline <xsd>]
                  java -jar xml-toolkit.jar scan --xsd <file>
                """);
    }
}

package com.project.toolkit.validate;

import org.xml.sax.SAXException;

import javax.xml.XMLConstants;
import javax.xml.transform.stream.StreamSource;
import javax.xml.validation.Schema;
import javax.xml.validation.SchemaFactory;
import javax.xml.validation.Validator;
import java.io.File;
import java.io.StringReader;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;

/**
 * Loads each XSD's compiled {@link Schema} once and reuses it for every validation call,
 * since compiling a schema is expensive and the toolkit validates thousands of files per run.
 */
public final class XsdValidatorCache {

    private static final Map<Path, Schema> CACHE = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    private XsdValidatorCache() {
    }

    public static Schema get(Path xsdPath) {
        return CACHE.computeIfAbsent(xsdPath, p -> {
            try {
                SchemaFactory factory = SchemaFactory.newInstance(XMLConstants.W3C_XML_SCHEMA_NS_URI);
                return factory.newSchema(new File(p.toString()));
            } catch (SAXException e) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid XSD: " + p + " -- " + e.getMessage(), e);
            }
        });
    }

    public static ValidationResult validate(Path xsdPath, Path xmlPath) {
        return validate(xsdPath, new StreamSource(xmlPath.toFile()));
    }

    /** Same as {@link #validate(Path, Path)} but for an XML document that only exists in memory
     * (e.g. a DTCC supplement fragment generated for A7, validated against its own XSD before
     * being embedded in the outer document) -- avoids a throwaway temp file for that check. */
    public static ValidationResult validateString(Path xsdPath, String xml) {
        return validate(xsdPath, new StreamSource(new StringReader(xml)));
    }

    private static ValidationResult validate(Path xsdPath, StreamSource source) {
        Schema schema = get(xsdPath);
        Validator validator = schema.newValidator();
        CollectingErrorHandler handler = new CollectingErrorHandler();
        validator.setErrorHandler(handler);
        try {
            validator.validate(source);
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return ValidationResult.fail(e.getMessage());
        }
        if (handler.hasErrors()) {
            return ValidationResult.fail(handler.firstMessage());
        }
        return ValidationResult.ok();
    }

    public record ValidationResult(boolean valid, String reason) {
        public static ValidationResult ok() {
            return new ValidationResult(true, null);
        }

        public static ValidationResult fail(String reason) {
            return new ValidationResult(false, reason);
        }
    }

    private static final class CollectingErrorHandler implements org.xml.sax.ErrorHandler {
        private String first;
        private int count;

        @Override
        public void warning(org.xml.sax.SAXParseException exception) {
        }

        @Override
        public void error(org.xml.sax.SAXParseException exception) {
            record(exception);
        }

        @Override
        public void fatalError(org.xml.sax.SAXParseException exception) {
            record(exception);
        }

        private void record(org.xml.sax.SAXParseException exception) {
            count++;
            if (first == null) {
                first = "line " + exception.getLineNumber() + ": " + exception.getMessage();
            }
        }

        boolean hasErrors() {
            return count > 0;
        }

        String firstMessage() {
            return first;
        }
    }
}
